screening_results.reason: This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants solving arithmetic word problems (a goal-directed problem-solving task). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (multiple regression), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and presents BOLD task-related activation results (tables/figures). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task definition (I5), whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinates reported (I7), BOLD/fMRI analysis (I8), and availability of voxelwise results in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes healthy-group task effects).

This study directly addresses task-based functional neuroimaging of problem solving using the Tower of London (a prototypical planning/problem-solving task requiring a goal and sequencing of moves). It reports both fMRI (BOLD) and PET (rCBF) analyses, with group-level voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses in healthy adult participants. The methods state transformation to stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) and reporting of coordinate-based statistical parametric maps; results describe task-related increases in specific brain regions (Brodmann areas) and thresholds, consistent with coordinate-based reporting. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a patient-group-only or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=19) using a goal-directed virtual-maze navigation task (find the pot with money). The task involves a clear goal and requires subjects to figure out routes, plan/sequentially execute directional choices and memorize egocentric cues—meeting the review’s operational definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (RFX–ANCOVA) and presents stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space for task-related activations (whole-brain maps and ROI analyses). BOLD (fMRI) signal changes and statistical maps are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, imaging acquisition, analysis), Results (tables/figures with coordinates), and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied.

The study is an event-related task-based fMRI experiment that directly examines problem-solving (word vs. number problems) in healthy adult participants. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with images normalized to MNI space, thresholding and contrasts (condition vs fixation, ANOVA), and describes task-related activations across brain regions; figures/tables are referenced for these results. BOLD fMRI acquisition and analyses are explicitly described. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for a whole-brain, task-based fMRI problem-solving study in healthy adults.

The study uses a first-person virtual maze where subjects have a goal and must determine routes/decisions to reach it, meeting the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (planning/sequencing/navigation). It includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses for healthy control participants, reports task-related BOLD results with stereotactic Talairach coordinates (e.g., 18 -61 40), and presents voxelwise whole-brain maps and VOI analyses. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of arithmetic problem solving in healthy adults that meets the review criteria. It directly examines problem solving (arithmetic operations requiring goal-directed operations and rule-based computation) meeting I5. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (I6). Data were normalized to MNI space and the manuscript indicates whole-brain contrast results are listed/depicted (satisfying I7 and I9). The study used BOLD fMRI (I8). Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of algebraic problem solving in healthy adults (N=18) that directly examines problem-solving strategies (symbolic vs. model) and the neural correlates of representing and validating solutions. It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses, BOLD fMRI data acquired on a 3T scanner, and states data were transformed into Talairach space with reported ROI maxima and activation clusters (results referenced in tables/figures). The study therefore meets the review’s requirements for a problem-solving task (I5), whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic reporting in Talairach space (I7), BOLD analysis (I8), and acceptable reporting of voxelwise results in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of verbal insight (chengyu) riddles in healthy adults, with event-related whole-brain GLM (random-effects) analyses and reported stereotactic peak coordinates. The task operationalizes problem solving by requiring participants to select a novel, reasonable answer (goal-directed solution selection involving constraint relaxation and representation change). Whole-brain activation contrasts (insight vs. rest, noninsight vs. rest, insight vs. noninsight) were performed and thresholded, group-level effects are reported, and peak coordinates are provided (via SPM preprocessing/normalization). Functional connectivity and ROI time-series were secondary but do not replace the whole-brain results. Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9; no exclusion criteria apply. No substantive missing core sections detected; full text appears complete.

Full text is a task-based fMRI study of solving Chinese logogriphs in healthy adults and reports BOLD-based whole-brain group contrasts of Successful vs Unsuccessful mental preparation. Inclusion met: I5 (problem-solving task: goal-directed riddle solving requiring analytic/semantic operations), I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion not met: I7 (the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space in the text; no coordinate tables or explicit coordinates are present in the supplied content), I9 (the main text does not clearly provide coordinates or explicitly indicate where voxelwise stereotactic coordinates are available in figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore exclude because it fails to meet I7 (and I9).

Excluded because the neuroimaging analysis is reported only in anatomically defined ROIs rather than as a whole-brain voxelwise/group-level stereotactic analysis. Specifically, the paper uses ROI-based SSI measures and manual ROI tracing and does not report stereotactic coordinates or whole-brain voxelwise coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI on a problem-solving task, Tower of London) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain analysis with group-level stereotactic results), I7 (no reported Talairach/MNI coordinates), and I9 (no indication that voxelwise stereotactic results are available in text/tables/supplement). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI results). Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the fMRI task is a reversal learning reward task, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no goal-directed planning/sequencing/critical-thinking problem-solving operations during the imaging task). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (results reported with small-volume/VOI correction focused on ventral striatum, i.e., effectively ROI-limited inference). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level/random-effects voxel-wise analyses in healthy adults were performed), I7 (stereotactic MNI coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results/figures provided). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not constitute a problem-solving task per the review definition). Full text appears complete.

The study employs a task (first-person virtual maze) that is goal-directed and requires participants to determine routes, plan and sequence navigational actions to reach the goal, meeting the review definition of a problem-solving task. It is a task-based fMRI study using BOLD signal (I8). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses for healthy control participants (DECIDE>BASELINE) in standardized Talairach space and refers to local maxima/tables of coordinates (I6, I7, I9). The analyses are voxelwise whole-brain (not ROI-only), and the healthy control task effects are explicitly reported, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines analogical reasoning, which involves goal-directed problem solving (identifying relational structure and selecting the correct response) and thus meets the review’s definition of problem solving. The study includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (with multiple-comparison correction), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise/peak results are reported in the main text. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adult participants examining arithmetic tasks (serial subtraction and multiplication recitation). It includes group-level whole-brain SPM analyses and reports rCBF task-related increases and activation maps (Brodmann areas). However, the supplied full text does not provide stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the text or tables; only Brodmann areas and referenced figures are reported. Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) is therefore not met based on the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Hence the study must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I7).

Excluded because the PASAT, while involving arithmetic and working memory, does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5) that requires evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions to reach a goal beyond routine one-digit arithmetic. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain PET group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates), I8 (rCBF PET analyses), and I9 (voxelwise/stereotactic results reported in tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Tables/References). Therefore excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that required participants to mentally solve integral calculus problems (a goal-directed problem-solving task involving rule-based operations, sequencing, and evaluation). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise thresholding (FDR q<.05), reports stereotactic coordinates (converted to Talairach space) and BOLD fMRI results in tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of four-term analogical reasoning (a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed inference and mapping). It recruited healthy adult participants (n=20) and performed group-level SPM analyses on BOLD data with whole-brain coverage. The paper reports stereotactic (MNI) activation coordinates (including RLPFC peaks) and task-related increases; voxelwise results and coordinates are presented. Although ROI analyses were used to characterize PFC effects, the study conducted whole-brain GLM preprocessing and group analyses and reports coordinate results. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices (matrix reasoning), which meets the review definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM) with task-related BOLD contrasts and tables/figures of stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. Healthy non-autistic adult control participants are included and their within-group task effects are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (a problem-solving task involving goal-directed sequencing and execution of operations). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (N=26), provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for task-related activations, and uses BOLD-fMRI analyses. The full text includes methods, results (whole-brain and ROI), and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based neuroimaging studies of problem solving and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of heuristic problem solving (simplified Sudoku) in healthy adults (n=15 analyzed). It uses whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA across conditions (group-level effects) and reports BOLD analyses. The data were coregistered to the Talairach coordinate system and the manuscript indicates ROI locations/sizes in the Appendix, satisfying stereotactic reporting. Voxelwise results are presented via figures/tables and multivariate classification results are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of fluid analogy-making in healthy adults (N=12) that operationalises problem solving via goal-directed analogy completion and selection among plausible solutions. It includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (FLAME), reports voxelwise task-related BOLD increases, and provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for significant clusters (e.g., BA 9 at −28,32,40 and BA45/46 at −39,32,26). Voxelwise cluster thresholds and BOLD % signal-change results are described. The study is empirical and the full text (Intro, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This is an original task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London problem-solving paradigm (meets I5). Participants were healthy adults (N=24) and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (meets I6). Functional images were normalized to MNI space and stereotactic peak coordinates/VOI peak coordinates are described and referenced (meets I7 and I9). The study used BOLD fMRI (3T EPI) and reports task-related hemodynamic effects (meets I8). Analyses include voxelwise whole-brain results (with thresholds and cluster extents) and are not limited to ROI-only findings. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of anagram problem solving (a goal-directed problem-solving task) in healthy adults, reporting group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses registered to MNI space and providing coordinate results (Table I). The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing, stimulus-locked voxelwise analyses, and cluster-thresholding; results include contrasts (aha-rest, search-rest, aha-search) with stereotactic activations. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used task-based fMRI on a problem-solving (simplified 4x4 Sudoku) paradigm in healthy elderly adults and reported BOLD signal results. However, the analysis was restricted to predefined ROIs in the bilateral PCC/precuneus (ROI-based percent signal change); no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) are reported. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis) and I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results). It also violates exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (problem-solving task), I8 (BOLD analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7 (and I9 not applicable). Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of mathematical problem solving in healthy adults (and adolescents), using whole-brain analyses and reporting BOLD-based results. It therefore satisfies I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain/group-level effects in healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD analysis). The manuscript includes whole-brain activation maps/figures, so I9 (accepting voxelwise results in figures/supplement) appears satisfied. However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) or explicitly state coordinate tables/supplementary coordinate lists; I7 is not met in the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not satisfied in the available full text, the study is excluded.

This is an fMRI task study of planning (Tower of London and navigation) in healthy adults that reports whole-brain BOLD contrasts and stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates (I5, I7, I8, I9 satisfied). However, it is a single-subject/case study (n=1) and does not include any group-level healthy adult effects; inclusion criterion I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults) is not met. Therefore it does not provide the group-level voxelwise results required for the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the study does not include any healthy-group task effect/group-level contrasts. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study of healthy adult participants performing a problem-solving task (Chinese chengyu riddles) that requires representation change, semantic retrieval, and selection of a solution—consistent with the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level random-effects analyses using whole-brain voxelwise SPM (no ROI-only restriction), BOLD (EPI-BOLD) measures, and stereotactic peak coordinates in MNI space for task contrasts (insight vs. noninsight) presented in the results. Both early (stimulus-locked) and late (response-locked) task-related BOLD contrasts are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/group-comparison-only, empirical healthy adult task data).

This is a task-based fMRI study of problem solving (Tower of London) in healthy adult participants (n=22). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with cluster-level correction across the whole brain, provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach space) and BOLD-related results, and includes voxelwise results in figures/tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (college students) that examines analogical reasoning—a problem-solving/complex reasoning task requiring identification and mapping of relationships and selection of correct responses. The study used whole-brain EPI acquisition, performed group-level whole-brain analysis in Talairach space, and reports task-related BOLD activation contrasts (analogy vs semantic and semantic vs baseline). Methods, results, and discussion are provided in full. Therefore it meets I5 (problem-solving/analogical reasoning task), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results in Talairach stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (results available via reported contrasts/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of anagram problem solving in healthy adult participants (N=15). The task meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed letter rearrangement requiring generation, evaluation, and planning of solutions). Whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses were performed (SPM2; normalization to MNI template) with voxelwise stereotactic coordinates reported for task-related BOLD activations. BOLD signal (fMRI) results are reported and coordinates are given in standard space. No exclusion criteria are violated. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

The study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). Although it is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results (see inclusion criteria I6, I7, I8, I9), the task is a virtual navigation/spatial memory learning paradigm focused on spatial vs. response strategies and habit learning. This is primarily a spatial memory/learning/navigation task rather than a domain-general problem-solving task involving critical evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions under explicit rule-based frameworks (semantic, algebraic, logical, etc.) as required by I5. Full text is complete and exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are not met.

The study uses task-based fMRI in healthy adult controls performing a Shepard–Metzler mental rotation task that requires holding a goal (same/different judgment) and performing mental operations to reach a correct judgment. This fits the review's problem-solving definition (spatial/problem-solving domain). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses including within-group (control) task effects and group comparisons. Results are reported with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach conversion) and voxelwise activation tables/figures. BOLD fMRI analysis is explicitly used. Voxelwise results are presented in tables and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports a task requiring participants to find novel shortcuts (a goal-directed task requiring planning, sequencing and deriving previously unknown solutions), which fits the review's definition of problem solving (I5). It is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain analyses (I6, I8). The methods state spatial normalization into MNI space and SPM analyses and report whole-brain statistical maps/activations (FWE-corrected) and anatomical localization, indicating stereotactic results are available (I7). The paper indicates voxelwise results are reported in maps/figures and likely tables (acceptable per I9). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not patient-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical).

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation using the Raven's Progressive Matrices, a problem-solving/analogical reasoning task (meets I5). It includes a healthy adult control group and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps for the control (NC) group and combined analyses (meets I6). Analyses were performed in MNI space and peak coordinates/locations are reported (meets I7). The study uses BOLD fMRI with voxelwise whole-brain results (meets I8). Task-related voxelwise results are reported in main text/figures and are available as stereotactic results (meets I9). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not solely disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), include healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E5), and it is empirical original data (not E6). Therefore the article should be INCLUDED.

This study used resting-state FDG-PET in OCD patients versus healthy controls; the PET acquisition was not task-based and no task-related imaging contrasts in healthy adults are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy adult participants), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (NOT a task-based fMRI/PET study of problem solving; PET was resting-state), I8 (does not report BOLD or rCBF task-related analyses; it reports glucose metabolism via FDG-PET). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study includes only between-group contrasts and does not report any healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study in 16 healthy adult subjects performing deductive and inductive reasoning tasks that fit the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed logical evaluation and execution of rule-based operations). The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM with spatial normalization to the MNI template and corrected voxelwise inference; BOLD (fMRI) contrasts for task effects are reported and results are summarized (with BA labels and implied coordinate tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only comparison, empirical healthy-adult task effects are presented). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This full text is complete. I exclude because it does not meet I5: the fMRI task was passive viewing of addition expressions with participants instructed to make no responses; although authors infer spontaneous/automatic calculation, participants were not engaged in an explicit problem-solving task (no goal-directed planning, sequencing, or execution to reach a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate results reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), and I9 (voxelwise results available in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task does not satisfy the review’s operational definition of a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore I exclude the study from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (BOLD) in healthy adult participants (N=14) using the Wason Selection Task, a logical deductive/problem-solving task that requires identifying/testing rule violations (fits problem-solving definition involving goal, evaluation, and rule-based operations). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and corrected thresholds, and also provides ROI analyses and stereotactic coordinates. Thus it meets I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, includes healthy-group task effects, and reports whole-brain results rather than only ROIs. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16) that examines analogical reasoning (fluid analogizing vs. symbol counting), which fits the operationalization of problem-solving (goal-directed evaluation and relational integration). The study reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (voxelwise Z-statistic images, thresholded, cluster-corrected), BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates (e.g., MNI 46,30,-12) with results presented across contrasts and ROI covariates. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

Although this article is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain analyses, stereotactic coordinates reported, and BOLD analyses (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), it does not meet the required definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The in-scanner task is a three-back working-memory/interference task (lure vs non-lure trials), which probes attentional control and working memory rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm as defined (involving evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions and executing operations to arrive at a novel solution). The Raven’s Progressive Matrices (a problem-solving measure) was administered outside the scanner and was not the task used during neuroimaging, so the neural data do not reflect task-based problem solving across domains. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=17) using a nonverbal analogy (People Pieces Analogy) task that requires goal-directed problem solving (identify relations, plan/evaluate, and execute a response), satisfying I5. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (mixed-effects), satisfying I6. Stereotactic coordinates are provided in MNI/Tables and figures, satisfying I7. The study reports BOLD fMRI results (BOLD/EPIs), satisfying I8. Voxelwise results are presented in tables and figures, satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), include healthy-group task effects (no E5), and it is empirical (no E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI investigation of deductive reasoning (conditional and relational tasks) in 12 healthy adult participants. Tasks require a goal (determine whether a conclusion follows) and involve logical operations and execution of rule-based inferences, meeting the review’s definition of problem solving. The analysis is whole-brain (EPI BOLD fMRI) with group-level results reported, Talairach stereotactic coordinates provided for activated ROIs, and task-related increases described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not rely solely on ROI-only reporting. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and the study should be included.

This study is an fMRI investigation of calendrical calculation and mental arithmetic and therefore meets I5 (task-based problem-solving-like tasks involving rule-based calculation), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). However, it does not meet I6: the paper does not report whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adult individuals — the imaging results are single-case/case-study (two autistic savants and a single normal participant) rather than a healthy adult group analysis. This violates the requirement for group-level healthy adult effects. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the study does not include a healthy-group task effect (no healthy adult group-level contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of algebra problem solving in healthy adult participants (N=20). It reports BOLD analyses and group-level task effects, conducts exploratory whole-brain analyses with reported Talairach coordinates for multiple regions (predefined ROIs and additional clusters), and presents task-related increases in brain activity. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review: I5 (task-based problem-solving task—algebra), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, modeling, and conclusions and appears complete. Hence INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants investigating analogical reasoning. The analogical task requires goal-directed evaluation and manipulation of relations (mapping and integration), which fits the review's problem-solving definition. The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses using SPM99, provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and voxel extents, and includes BOLD contrast results. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only reports, not a patient/group comparison only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and experimental procedures present).

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London (a well-established problem-solving/planning task) with healthy control participants. It reports whole-brain group-level SPM analyses in healthy adults (group activation maps), BOLD analyses, and data were co-registered into MNI space with thresholded activation maps and subtraction maps (figures) making stereotactic-space results available. Voxelwise/cluster results are presented as maps and Brodmann-area-localized clusters (figures/tables referenced), meeting the allowance that coordinate/voxelwise results may be reported in figures. The study is not ROI-only and includes within-group healthy task effects. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for problem-solving task fMRI in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study using mental arithmetic (three-digit addition/subtraction), which qualifies as a problem-solving task involving goal-directed calculation, planning/sequencing and rule-based operations. It includes a healthy control group with group-level whole-brain analyses (one-sample t-tests in controls and ANCOVA), reports task-related BOLD results, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of methods and results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, not solely disease/age/gender comparisons, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of deductive reasoning (conditional and relational arguments), which qualifies as problem-solving within a logical/semantic rule framework. Participants were healthy adults (final N=13). The study conducted whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM5) and reports voxelwise stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. BOLD fMRI (T2*-weighted) was used and task-related activations are reported in the text and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving/logical reasoning task), I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mathematical problem solving in healthy adult participants (N=20 university students). It reports group-level BOLD analyses, whole-brain classification (MVPA) and an exploratory whole-brain contrast with cluster tables referenced, and provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach coordinates reported for angular gyrus and HIPS coordinates used). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem-solving fMRI), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analyses), and I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results available in tables/figures). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results, it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The experimental task is subliminal relational/analogy detection and semantic fit judgments, focusing on unconscious memory/analogy mapping rather than on goal-directed problem solving involving evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions, or executing operations to reach a (novel) solution. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete.

While this is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates, the experimental tasks are virtual navigation and memory/strategy learning (4/8VM and CSDLT) assessing hippocampus vs caudate-dependent spatial vs response strategies. These tasks probe memory and navigational strategy selection rather than problem-solving as defined for the meta-analysis (i.e., tasks requiring goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing operations within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical or similar rule-based frameworks to arrive at a novel solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. The manuscript otherwise meets I6, I7, I8 (and I9 as coordinates/results are reported), and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adult participants performing arithmetic (multiplication) verification, which qualifies as a problem-solving task (goal-directed operations to arrive at correct solutions). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM5, provides stereotactic (MNI) coordinates for task-related activation (e.g., left angular gyrus peak), and uses BOLD fMRI. Coordinate and voxelwise results are reported and validated with regression and ROI follow-ups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all included criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study of geometric analogical problem solving in healthy adults (mean age 18.7). The task requires goal-directed problem solving (identifying and mapping relations to reach a correct judgment) meeting the review's problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analyses (FLAME) with cluster thresholds, BOLD-based fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates for activated regions (e.g., RLPFC coordinates), and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based PET study of the Tower of London problem-solving task (meets I5). It includes healthy adult controls with group-level task effects and whole-brain analyses (I6). Results report regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) PET analyses (I8) and provide stereotactic peak coordinates after normalization to a standard stereotaxic space (I7). Voxelwise/peak results are described in the text and tables/peaks are reported (I9). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, includes healthy task effects, not a review). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based, event-related BOLD fMRI study of insight problem solving in healthy adult participants, with group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses comparing Aha vs No-aha conditions. It therefore meets I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for the task-related activations; only Brodmann areas and region labels are listed and the manuscript refers to summary figures/tables that are not included in the supplied content. Because I7 (reports stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach or MNI space) is not satisfied in the provided material, the study cannot be included for coordinate-based meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD-fMRI study of problem solving in healthy adults (N=17). Participants performed a defined problem-solving task (learning prototypes then solving scientific innovation problems), satisfying I5. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (contrast HFF>OHFF) in healthy adults, satisfying I6. Imaging data were normalized to Talairach space and peak coordinates/cluster tables are reported, satisfying I7 and I9. The study reports BOLD fMRI results (task-related increases), satisfying I8. The full text provided contains introduction, methods (participants, tasks, imaging acquisition/analysis), results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET study of healthy adult participants (n=12) using a modified Tower of London task that requires goal-setting, planning, sequencing moves, and execution — meeting the review’s definition of problem-solving (I5). Analyses were performed at the group level across the whole brain (PET images normalized to a stereotaxic coordinate system), reporting stereotactic peak coordinates (x,y,z) and voxelwise rCBF results, satisfying I6, I7, and I8. Coordinate results and statistical maps are presented in the text/tables, consistent with I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs (E3), are not only between-group/disease comparisons (E4/E5), and the paper is original empirical research (not a review) (E6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study in healthy adults that investigates maze traversal — a goal-directed task requiring planning, sequencing, and execution (meets I5). The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses using SPM across 11 healthy adult participants (meets I6), provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates for task-related activations (meets I7), and reports regional cerebral blood flow PET results (meets I8). Voxelwise/statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables are presented in the results (meets I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not ROI-only, not limited to disease/age/gender contrasts, include healthy-group task effects, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults (n=20) using the paced serial addition task (PASAT/PVSAT). The task involves rule-based arithmetic operations (adding the current digit to the previous) requiring working memory, rule-based execution and goal-directed calculation, which fits the review’s definition of problem-solving (I5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (FLAME) in healthy adults (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and cluster maxima (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI contrasts (I8). Coordinate reporting in figures/tables is available (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (young female participants) using problem-solving/reasoning tasks (induction, visualization, spatial relationships) that require selecting the correct missing figure — meeting the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level analyses (random effects), BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach examples and reported peak coordinates). Voxelwise results are presented in maps/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so completeness is sufficient.

This is an fMRI study of deductive (logical) reasoning in healthy adults with whole-brain group analyses and BOLD-based results; however, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations or provide coordinate tables/figures in the excerpt. Inclusion criterion I7 (reports stereotactic coordinate results) is not satisfied based on the supplied content. The full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study cannot be included under the meta-analysis rules that require coordinate reporting.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a virtual-maze navigation task that requires a goal (find way out) and planning/sequencing of actions to reach it, meeting the review's problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level (random-effects) analyses in 24 healthy adults, stereotactic coordinates (Talairach), and BOLD fMRI results presented in tables/figures. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical data reported). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of the Tower of London problem-solving task in healthy adults (n=22). The study performed whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with FWE correction after normalization to MNI space, reporting task-related activations; BOLD EPI data were acquired and analyzed. Although an ROI approach was used for some analyses, whole-brain voxelwise results were explicitly reported and used to define ROIs, so the study is not ROI-only. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based problem-solving), I6 (whole-brain group effects in healthy adults), I7 (MNI stereotactic normalization/coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The virtual maze and spatial-learning tasks assess spatial memory and navigation (encoding/retrieval of landmark positions, viewpoint shifts, path integration) rather than explicit problem solving that requires goal-directed planning/sequencing operations within a defined rule set (e.g., semantic, algebraic, logical operations). The study does, however, meet other imaging-related inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study reporting whole-brain group-level analyses (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in standardized space (MNI) (I7), reports BOLD fMRI results (I8), and presents voxelwise results in text/tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that uses goal-directed rule-discovery and analogy tasks requiring generation of structured representations and mapping to select correct targets — processes consistent with problem solving as defined (identifying rules, planning/performing rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, presents stereotactic MNI coordinates for activation peaks, and BOLD-based analyses. Voxelwise results and ROI checks are described in the main text. No exclusion criteria apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical PET study in 15 healthy adult volunteers using H2(15)O PET with whole-brain SPM voxelwise analyses comparing naive vs practiced maze performance. The maze task requires a goal (reach end), planning/sequencing and problem solving via trial-and-error and feedback to discover and follow the correct path, satisfying the review's definition of problem solving. The paper reports group-level rCBF results in stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates (examples given for hippocampal/parahippocampal activations) and includes whole-brain analyses and rCBF measures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions).

The study uses a probabilistic reversal learning task (reinforcement learning) and analyzes ventral striatal prediction error signals. While it meets several technical imaging criteria (group-level whole-brain GLM, stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD analyses), the task does not fit the meta-analysis definition of a 'problem solving' task (goal-directed complex planning, sequencing operations, or critical-thinking to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI results) are strictly triggered, as a whole-brain GLM was performed (though main inferences used SVC in VS). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. The tactile multiple T-maze is a goal-directed task requiring planning/sequencing and rule-based navigation (meets I5). The paper reports task-based BOLD fMRI with group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants (congenitally blind and blindfolded sighted controls) (meets I6 and I8). Results are reported with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and coordinate tables/figures (meets I7 and I9). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, and analyses include whole-brain contrasts and group comparisons rather than ROI-only results. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adult abacus experts and controls performing goal-directed mental-operation tasks (numeral arithmetic, spatial manipulation, verbal sequencing) that require planning/operations under rule sets to reach correct responses, meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM (healthy adults), provides stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases (x,y,z in standard space), and uses BOLD fMRI. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Wason selection task (deductive/problem-solving). The task meets the review's problem-solving definition (goal-driven selection of cards to detect rule violations; requires logical evaluation, planning/strategy, and rule-constrained operations). Methods report whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (second-level paired t tests and conjunctions), voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and BOLD fMRI acquisition/analyses. Results include coordinate-based activation tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This task meets the review definition of problem solving: participants had an explicit goal (collect hidden rewards) and had to figure out and execute navigation strategies (use extra-maze cues, plan routes, avoid revisiting arms), involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and rule-based operations (don’t re-enter arms). The study used task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI with group-level random effects analyses (N=25 healthy adults), normalized to an MNI template and reporting activation maps/tables, satisfying whole-brain coordinate reporting. Voxelwise results and contrasts (A vs B, A vs C, reward/no-reward) are reported. Thus I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports a task-based BOLD fMRI experiment in healthy adults using a virtual maze navigation task that requires participants to form an allocentric ‘cognitive map’ and select the correct map (goal-directed behavior requiring translation/representation and selection), which meets the problem-solving definition (goal + need to determine a way to reach it and execute an action to select the correct map). The paper includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, reports stereotactic coordinates, and provides ROI analyses in addition to voxelwise results. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a goal-directed virtual navigation task that required learning object locations and planning routes (meets the review’s problem-solving definition, I5). The study performed voxel-wise, whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants (I6) using BOLD fMRI (I8). The manuscript reports standardized stereotactic activation results (BA clusters and references to cluster coordinates/figures/tables), satisfying I7 and I9. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core content present). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects in healthy adults).

This fMRI study uses a virtual navigation (T-maze) task and reports whole-brain BOLD group analyses with MNI coordinates in healthy adults, so it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the experimental task is spatial navigation with simple left/right choices for reward (with feedback determined randomly) and auxiliary assessments of spatial ability. It does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or executing operations within a rule-based framework to derive solutions. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (with concurrent EEG) of a problem-solving task (Chinese character chunk decomposition) in healthy adult participants. It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects fMRI analyses using BOLD contrast, presents voxelwise stereotactic coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) and cluster results, and provides behavioral and imaging results across conditions. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, procedure, fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical-group comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI (BOLD) study in healthy adults that examines goal-directed, context-dependent navigation requiring retrieval, evaluation, planning and sequencing of actions (disambiguation of overlapping routes), which fits the review's operational definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level, whole-brain analyses (random-effects SPMs), uses MNI normalization and provides stereotactic coordinates and cluster results for task contrasts and connectivity differences, and presents BOLD-based beta-series correlation connectivity results. All required reporting formats (whole-brain results, coordinates in standardized space, BOLD analysis) are present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not clinical or non-empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD-fMRI study of numerical inductive reasoning, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (identifying a rule from a number series and generating the next number). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (within-group task vs rest and between-group comparisons) using SPM8, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (figures and supplementary tables), and uses BOLD-fMRI. Participants were healthy adult groups (young and elderly) screened for cognitive impairment. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of deductive (syllogistic) reasoning in healthy adults, which qualifies as problem-solving under the review definition (logical operations to reach a conclusion). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM, provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) and BOLD-based fMRI results, and includes voxelwise activation tables and time-course analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using the Tower of London planning/problem-solving task (goal-directed planning). Whole-brain, random-effects group analyses are reported (ANOVA, random-effects), with voxelwise stereotactic coordinates given in MNI (and converted to Talairach) and task-related BOLD results. Voxelwise results are reported and thresholds described. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses a goal-directed virtual 8-arm radial maze requiring participants to learn and plan routes, avoid revisiting arms (rule-based sequencing/execution), and thus meets the operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). It includes healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (omnibus F test) with reported stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I6, I7). The imaging modality is BOLD fMRI with voxelwise results presented in figures/tables (I8, I9). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only reporting, healthy-group task effects are present, and this is original empirical data).

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of categorical vs. coordinate spatial encoding during active navigation in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is spatial memory/navigation encoding, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review—there is no focus on identifying/performing critical thinking processes to evaluate a problem, plan/sequencing actions to derive a solution within semantic/algebraic/logical frameworks), and I7 (the provided full text does not clearly report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space in the text supplied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the key problem-solving task requirement (I5) and does not clearly report stereotactic coordinates in the supplied content (I7).

The study uses a task in which subjects must mentally navigate from one place to another, requiring a goal and planning/sequencing of turns (meets problem-solving definition). It is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants (16 right-handed males) with group-level whole-brain random-effects analysis. The paper reports activation peaks (voxelwise results) across subjects, which implies stereotactic coordinate reporting (results/peaks/tables/figures available), and BOLD signal analysis was used. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group/disease comparison only, and not non-empirical). Although explicit coordinate numbers are not shown in the provided excerpt, the text states detected peaks and group-level random-effects results, consistent with inclusion criterion I7/I9. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study of deductive reasoning (conditional and syllogistic problems) in healthy adults (n=26). The tasks require goal-directed, rule-based problem solving (logical integration to derive conclusions), meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM2, BOLD (fMRI) results, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures and supplementary maps). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I9). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (12 subjects) using a sequential planning/game task (Hit-N) that requires goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions under rules (move 1–3 or 1–4 positions), and execution to reach a target — meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses (event-related rfxGLM) in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic results in Talairach space and provides coordinate figures/maps (I7, I9), and reports task-related BOLD effects (I8). Analyses include whole-brain contrasts (not ROI-only) with voxelwise results and statistical maps (FDR q<0.05 and uncorrected thresholds), with methods and preprocessing described. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures), so inclusion is appropriate.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=23) using series-completion inductive reasoning tasks that meet the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed rule identification and execution to arrive at a previously unknown solution). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the full text. The study is not limited to ROI-only results and includes voxelwise whole-brain contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning/problem-solving task (meets problem-solving definition). It reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activation foci, and uses BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are reported and visualized. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is task-based fMRI of a planning/problem-solving task (Tower of London) in healthy adults with group-level random-effects analysis and reports BOLD results; however, the provided full text does not include stereotactic (Talairach or MNI) coordinates for task-related activations. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no coordinates reported in provided text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete but lacks explicit coordinate tables or numerical stereotactic results required for inclusion.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study using H2 15O measuring regional cerebral blood flow during the Tower of London planning task (a problem-solving paradigm). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM (normalization to stereotaxic space) and lists activation tables/figures (stereotactic coordinates referenced to standard space). Participants are healthy adults (n=6). rCBF analyses are reported and correlational/contrast results are presented. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based PET problem-solving studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults using the PASAT, an arithmetic problem-solving task (adding consecutive digits) that fits the review’s definition of problem solving (rule-based algebraic operations, planning/sequencing, execution). It reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, voxelwise activation maps and tables, stereotactic coordinates (MNI transformed to Talairach), and BOLD fMRI results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults using a goal-directed virtual navigation task (CSDLT) in which participants must determine which path contains an object—requiring goal-directed selection, evaluation of landmarks, and sequencing of actions. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise BOLD analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and presents BOLD results (fMRI contrasts and correlations) and VBM analyses. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task involves goal-directed problem-solving-like processes in a navigational domain), I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Caveat: the task is spatial/navigation learning rather than classical abstract problem-solving; inclusion is based on the meta-analysis definition that encompasses goal-directed planning/sequence actions to reach a goal.

This is a task-based fMRI study of matrix problem solving (Raven-like) in 34 healthy adult participants. The task meets the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed matrix reasoning with rule-based operations and correct-response selection). The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected) and provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) and tables/figures of activations. BOLD fMRI is the imaging modality. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions) is present and appears complete.

This study is an fMRI investigation of mental subtraction in healthy adults and reports group-level activation differences and BOLD EPI data (meets I5 and I8). However, it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis: (1) Whole-brain coverage/analysis (I6) appears not satisfied — imaging used only 10 slices parallel to AC–PC, suggesting limited brain coverage rather than whole-brain analysis; (2) No stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) are reported in the full text (I7); (3) No voxelwise stereotactic coordinates are provided in text/tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I6/I7/I9 are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using mental arithmetic (subtraction and multiplication), which constitutes an algebraic/problem-solving task per the review definition. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, BOLD signal contrasts, conjunction analyses, voxelwise pattern correlations, and uses stereotactic normalization to MNI space with reference to peak voxels and spheres around them (indicating coordinate-based results are reported in the main text/figures). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study in healthy adult participants that directly examines complex mental calculation (a problem-solving task defined by goal-directed operations under arithmetic rules) and a visuospatial N-Back task. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses on PET rCBF data, provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI), and presents task-related increases in NrCBF (voxelwise results described in the text and figures). All inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are met. No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This empirical fMRI study (n=16 healthy adults) examines wayfinding/route-following tasks that require a goal and computing/planning routes to reach targets, which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates for task-related activations (MNI/Talairach) (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (T2*-weighted) (I8), and presents voxelwise results in the text/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only group comparisons by disease/age/sex, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not study a problem-solving task (I5 not met). The fMRI task is an emotion/mood induction using IAPS, not goal-directed problem solving or critical-thinking/planning operations. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). This is a task-based fMRI study of arithmetic problem solving (single-digit addition), which qualifies as a problem-solving task (goal-directed computation and execution of operations within a rule set), satisfying I5. Although this fMRI study used whole-brain group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adults and reports stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, the task does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). Tasks meet the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed problem solving with rule-based operations and execution). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment using the paced visual serial addition task (PVSAT), which involves goal-directed, rule-based arithmetic operations (satisfying the review's broad definition of problem solving). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical human data).

This is a task-based fMRI study of planning/problem solving (Tower of London) in healthy adults (N=17). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study uses whole-brain task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adults (meets I6 and I8) and reports voxelwise activation contrasts in the main text (consistent with I9). While goal-directed, it is primarily an information-retrieval/memory and perceptual-motor task rather than a domain-general problem-solving paradigm as defined by I5 (involving critical evaluation, planning/sequencing operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule-sets to arrive at a novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply to this study based on the available information.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation using an abstract reasoning task that requires identifying the next item in a sequence (goal-directed problem solving via pattern detection, planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a correct response), meeting the review’s operational definition of problem solving. It includes whole-brain, group-level analyses for both alcohol-dependent and healthy adult control groups (one-sample t tests and between-group tests), reports BOLD results, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-empirical, or absence of healthy-group task effects) are met.

The study uses task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adults performing goal-directed navigation that explicitly includes self-localization, target localization, path planning and execution—meeting the review’s definition of problem solving. Group-level whole-brain analyses (FLAME1) are reported, with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates provided (e.g., 25, -20, -18) and BOLD results described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient/group-comparison-only, empirical with healthy-task effects). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study uses a paced visual serial addition task (PVSAT/PASAT) which requires applying an arithmetic rule to compute consecutive sums (goal-directed, rule-conforming operations involving working memory and executive control), meeting the review’s definition of problem-solving. It reports a whole-brain, random-effects group analysis in healthy adult participants (n=9), uses task-based BOLD fMRI, and presents stereotactic coordinates referenced to Talairach space in tables/figures. Voxelwise results are provided in group-level tables and figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Caveat: the task is a highly constrained arithmetic/attention task rather than open-ended problem solving, but it satisfies the inclusion criteria as defined.

While this study reports whole-brain, group-level task-based fMRI results in healthy adults (BOLD fMRI) with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and voxelwise analyses, the experimental paradigm is a spatial learning/navigation task (virtual maze encoding and retrieval) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., requiring goal-directed planning/sequencing of actions or rule-based operations to arrive at a novel solution). The task mainly assesses spatial memory and inference of relative positions following passive traversal, not the types of active problem-solving processes (evaluating options, planning sequences of actions, applying semantic/algebraic/logical rules) specified in I5. Therefore I5 is not met, so the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of logical problem solving (identifying contradictions using Aristotelian premise-conclusion pairs) in healthy adult participants. The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects fMRI analyses (SPM8), BOLD results, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related increases. The experimental task fits the problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical evaluation and application of rule set). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a goal-directed virtual navigation/place-learning task that requires subjects to plan/sequence actions to retrieve objects (meets problem-solving definition). It reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses (n=14) with statistical maps and tables, provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates for peak activations, and includes voxelwise results in tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a clinical-group-only comparison, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria below are satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines complex arithmetic tasks requiring multi-step calculation (working memory, planning/sequencing) consistent with the review's definition of problem solving.
