Task-related increases are reported in the text/figures/tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that required goal-directed planning, sequencing, and execution to reach a hidden goal (encoding a map, planning a route, using self-motion cues to navigate). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t tests and contrasts), uses BOLD fMRI, normalizes data to MNI space (coordinates/tables provided), and presents voxelwise results in tables and figures. The task meets the review definition of problem solving (goal plus need to compute and execute actions to reach it). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes explicit route-planning tasks (customer-driven route planning) that meet the review's definition of problem solving: subjects are given a goal and must plan/sequence actions to reach it. The study used whole-brain, group-level analyses (random-effects SPM2), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and presents BOLD-based results (EPI BOLD contrast) with tables of activations. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-group-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD stereotactic coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task is associative memory/label identification (learned mapping of four chords to numerals) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed generation/planning/sequencing of novel solutions or critical evaluation operations). The task involves retrieval of learned conditional associations and motor responses, not formulation or execution of strategies to solve a presented problem. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study does not satisfy the required problem-solving task criterion (I5) and must be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that meets the review’s problem-solving definition: participants had an explicit goal (find a hidden goal in a virtual starmaze) and had to plan/choose actions (place- or sequence-based strategies) to reach it. The study reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses (N=17; additional connectivity analyses in N=13) with stereotactic coordinates provided in MNI space, and voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be INCLUDED.

The study uses an anagram task that requires goal-directed problem solving (identifying/arranging letters to find words), meeting the operational definition of problem solving. It is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (mixed-effects ANOVA) with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related activations (main effect of condition and group x condition interaction). ROI analyses are supplementary. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of problem solving/insight in healthy adults. It uses an event-related fMRI paradigm where participants attempt to associate heuristic prototypes with previously learned technical problems (a goal-directed problem-solving/insight task). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects contrasts (RP > UP), uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic results in Talairach space (locations and Brodmann areas reported). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I9 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Although the study meets several methodological criteria for inclusion (whole-brain group analyses, stereotactic (MNI) coordinate reporting, task-based BOLD fMRI, and voxelwise results availability), it does not meet the review’s definitional inclusion criterion I5. The in-scanner task is a Hayling sentence completion/verbal fluency paradigm probing executive and semantic retrieval processes, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing operations within a rule set to reach a correct or novel solution). The paper’s emphasis is on emotion, executive/fluency and risk for mood disorder rather than problem-solving across domains in healthy adults. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) .

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants that investigates goal-directed navigation requiring participants to plan and select sequences of actions to reach maze goals. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and BOLD fMRI results (multiple whole-brain tables/figures). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full article text (methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This task-based fMRI study uses the PASAT, a rule-based, goal-directed arithmetic task involving planning/sequencing and execution (meets problem-solving definition). This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly probes mechanical problem solving by requiring participants to infer function-from-structure and plan/execute pantomimes for unfamiliar tools (goal-directed inference and planning). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is available. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study of problem solving using the Tower of Toronto (isomorphous to Tower of Hanoi) in healthy adults. This is a task-based fMRI study of numerical inductive reasoning using a number-series completion task that requires identifying underlying rules and generating solutions — matching the review definition of problem solving. This is a task-based fMRI study using Raven's Progressive Matrices (a problem-solving/fluid reasoning task), with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) and group-level within-group effects reported for the healthy comparison group. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., results are not ROI-only, healthy-group task effects are reported).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of deductive problem solving (syllogisms) in healthy adults. It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM8 with normalization to MNI space and voxelwise BOLD contrasts (integration effect), provides stereotactic coordinates (e.g. −42 14 20), and reports significant task-related activations (voxel-level FWE-corrected). Thus it satisfies I5–I9. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of complex arithmetic in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and BOLD fMRI results (meets I5, I6, I8). However, the provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinate listings for the reported activation peaks, and there is no clear presentation of voxelwise coordinates in the supplied content (does not meet I7). The text also does not provide coordinate results in tables/figures or indicate their availability in supplementary material within the provided file (does not meet I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore I must exclude the study because not all required inclusion criteria (I7 and I9) are satisfied in the supplied full text.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants examining mental calculation (exact and compound arithmetic). Mental calculation fits the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed, rule-based operations, planning/sequencing such as decomposition/recomposition strategies). The study reports whole-brain group-level SPM analyses (fixed-effects across subjects), uses BOLD fMRI, and reports stereotactic results referenced to a standard template (MNI normalization) with coordinates in tables/figures. Voxelwise results are presented in tables and figures. It is not an ROI-only study, not a clinical group-comparison, and is not a review. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete for screening purposes. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=10) using mental arithmetic (subtraction and multiplication), which constitutes a problem-solving task under rule-based operations (arithmetic procedures and retrieval). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (FWE-corrected cluster-level threshold) and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (e.g., left hIPS x=−37,y=−48,z=49 and right hIPS x=44,y=−45,z=54). BOLD fMRI was used and task-related activations are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem-solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (coordinates/results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusion).

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of mental arithmetic (a problem-solving task involving goal-directed calculation and rule-based operations) in 20 healthy adult participants. It includes whole-brain, group-level analyses (second-level SPM), reports BOLD results, and provides stereotactic coordinates for task-related activations (Talairach/MNI-style coordinates) in tables/figures. Voxelwise results are reported and discussed. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=13) using a goal-directed maze navigation task that requires planning, sequential decision-making, and execution to reach a goal (qualifies as problem-solving). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (random-effects) were performed, BOLD fMRI was used, and stereotactic coordinates are reported (e.g., MNI x,y,z = -32,49,-1). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not group-comparison-only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inductive reasoning (number-series problems) in healthy adults that requires identifying and applying rules to generate previously unknown solutions, fitting the review’s definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM analyses (SI vs. control; CI vs. SI), uses BOLD fMRI, and normalized data to MNI space. Results describe stereotactic activations (with ROI definitions and contrasts; coordinates are indicated as available in results/figures/tables), and analyses include voxelwise contrasts with correction. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/group-comparison only, and is empirical). Full text includes intro, methods, results, discussion and conclusions; supplemental material is not required. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16) that examines deductive/transitive reasoning (logical validity judgments), which qualifies as a problem-solving task (goal-directed evaluation using rule-based logic). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM2) and discusses stereotactic results (MNI coordinates/Z-values) with imaging results reported in the manuscript (tables/figures referenced). All required inclusion criteria are met (I5: problem-solving logical task; I6: whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults; I7: stereotactic coordinate results in MNI space; I8: BOLD fMRI analysis; I9: coordinates/results available in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are triggered: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to disease/age/gender contrasts, and include within-group healthy task effects. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore include.

Exclusion E5 applies: the paper only reports between-group contrasts (higher vs lower mathematical competence) as the primary whole-brain results and does not report whole-group (task > baseline) healthy adult task effects. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task involves goal-directed problem evaluation and arithmetic operations), I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20) that used arithmetic tasks (exact and approximate calculation, magnitude comparison). These tasks involve goal-directed, rule-based problem solving (selecting/calculating correct sums or magnitude comparisons) and thus meet the review's problem-solving definition. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise BOLD analyses (SPM99) with FWE/FDR correction and between- and within-group statistical maps; stereotactic coordinates are given (MNI transformed to Talairach). Group-level effects for healthy adults are reported. Full-text includes methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy adult task effects). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study of three-term relational reasoning (a logical problem-solving task requiring subjects to determine whether conclusions follow from premises), conducted in 14 healthy adult subjects with group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses using SPM. The methods explicitly describe whole-brain preprocessing and voxelwise inference after normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template, and the results section references voxelwise activations summarized in tables/figures (stereotactic results are indicated as available). The study reports BOLD (T2*-weighted) analyses and task-related activation increases. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a review, includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and is eligible for inclusion.

This study reports task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants performing calculation tasks that involve rule-based operations (exact and approximate arithmetic), which fit the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed operations using algebraic/semantic rules to arrive at correct/approximate solutions). The paper includes group-level adult task effects (within-group math > control contrasts), reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space, and presents BOLD results. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This is a task-based fMRI empirical study of fluid-reasoning/problem-solving tasks (Induction and Visualization) in healthy adult participants (N=22, ages 20–24). The tasks are problem-solving in nature (goal-directed reasoning with rule-based responses). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain analyses (seed-based whole-brain correlation maps and voxelwise contrasts), provides stereotactic coordinates transformed to Talairach space, and uses BOLD fMRI measures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not merely abstract/metadata). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied.

This PET study uses a task (phonological verbal fluency) that meets the review's problem-solving definition: it has a goal (generate words), a rule set (words must begin with a specific letter), and requires planning/sequencing and execution to retrieve words. The study includes healthy adult controls and presents whole-brain, voxelwise rCBF (PET) analyses with group-level effects. Task-related activations are reported with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach). Voxelwise results and coordinate maxima are reported in the text/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. The participant sample comprises adolescents (ages 12–18), including clinical (autism) and sibling groups, not healthy adults — therefore I6 (healthy adult group-level effects) is not met. The task (Embedded Figures Task) is a perceptual visual search/shape-detection paradigm and does not clearly meet the review’s defined construct of multi-domain problem solving involving planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a goal — therefore I5 is not met. The full text is complete and reports whole-brain BOLD analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and figures/tables, so I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are specifically triggered by the content. Given the age group and task mismatch to the meta-analysis objective, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that uses an arithmetic (addition) manipulation task requiring participants to compute sums (a goal-directed operation using rule-based arithmetic procedures), satisfying the meta-analysis definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses of BOLD data, uses MNI stereotactic space for localization, and provides activation foci (coordinates) and statistical thresholds. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a syllogistic logical reasoning task (goal-directed problem solving within a logical rule set), meeting the review’s operational definition of problem solving (I5). Whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses were performed on healthy adult participants (N=15 for imaging analyses) with standard preprocessing and group ANOVAs (I6). Results report stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (e.g., MNI coordinates provided for hippocampus, superior temporal gyrus, thalamus, etc.) and voxelwise thresholding procedures (I7). The study uses BOLD fMRI (1.5T Siemens VISION; BOLD contrast) (I8). Voxelwise results are reported in the main text and in Supplementary Tables/Figures (I9). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary material referenced but not required for eligibility. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes the Tower of London planning task (a well-defined problem-solving/planning paradigm) and a 2-back working memory task. It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adult controls and patients, provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) for task-related increases, and analyzes BOLD signal changes. Results (tables/figures) present voxelwise coordinate findings and pooled whole-brain contrasts. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-empirical, or lacking healthy-group task effects) are met.

This is an fMRI BOLD study including a healthy control group and whole-brain group-level analyses, and it examines calculation (two-digit addition/subtraction) which fits the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (I5). It reports group-level whole-brain SPM analyses for healthy adults (I6) and BOLD fMRI (I8). However, the provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in tables, figures, or supplementary listings that are accessible here; criterion I7 (reporting coordinates) is not satisfied based on the available text. Because reporting of stereotactic coordinates is required for inclusion, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) but coordinate data are not present in the provided content; if coordinates are present in figures/supplementary materials not provided, this decision may change.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based BOLD fMRI study using a subtraction task that requires complex problem solving (borrowing/estimation), satisfying I5. It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and presents group activation maps for healthy adult controls (age 20-26), satisfying I6. Results are reported in Talairach stereotactic space (I7) and include BOLD-related regression coefficients/percent signal change (I8). Voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables (I9). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only (whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported), healthy-group task effects are presented, and this is an empirical human neuroimaging study. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain, task-based fMRI studies of problem-solving in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of imagined egocentric transformations (hand and perspective rotation) in healthy adults. While it includes whole-brain, group-level analyses reported in MNI space and BOLD results, the tasks are mental rotation/spatial-visualization and handedness/left–right judgments rather than goal-directed problem-solving as defined in the review (i.e., requiring identification/planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution within a rule-based problem-solving framework). Therefore it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in adults using a goal-directed wayfinding task that requires planning/sequencing to find the shortest route (meets I5). The paper includes healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain analyses (within-group and between-group effects) (meets I6). Images were normalized to ICBM templates and SPM analyses were conducted; the manuscript references result tables/figures for reported activations (indicating stereotactic reporting in standardized space per I7 and allowed under I9). BOLD (fMRI) analyses are explicitly reported (meets I8). The study is not ROI-only and includes whole-brain results and healthy-group task effects, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and appears complete. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for this review and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=18 analyzed) using a computational estimation arithmetic task that requires goal-directed problem solving (selecting/evaluating and executing strategies), satisfying I5. The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (SPM, group one-sample and paired t-tests), meeting I6. Images were normalized to MNI space and ROI coordinates are provided; the text references tables/figures of voxelwise activations (indicating stereotactic results are reported), supporting I7 and I9. BOLD-sensitive EPI acquisition and BOLD analyses are described, satisfying I8. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only results, no patient-group-only contrasts, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants performing complex multiplication problems that require goal-directed calculation and rule-based operations (meets I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise results and statistical maps/tables are reported (I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (E3–E6 not met). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as a whole-brain task-based fMRI investigation of problem-solving in healthy adults.

This study is a task-based whole-brain fMRI investigation in healthy adults that includes a mental-arithmetic task (serial addition) which involves rule-based operations to arrive at correct numeric results, fitting the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (algebraic/operational processes). The paper reports group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (young and old groups), voxelwise BOLD results with stereotactic MNI coordinates, and provides task-related BOLD contrasts. Methods, results and coordinates are presented in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes within-group task effects, not solely a between-group/disease study). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a problem-solving paradigm (adapted Raven’s Progressive Matrices) in healthy adults, meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed reasoning, rule inference, planning/sequencing, and selecting a correct solution). It reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, voxelwise BOLD results, and stereotactic Talairach coordinates for activations. Voxelwise/whole-brain maps and ROI analyses are described; whole-brain results are present and not limited to ROIs. The sample consists of healthy adult participants. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in stereotactic (Talairach) space (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), the experimental task is simple arithmetic fact retrieval (multiplication verification) aimed at retrieval of stored solutions rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires planning, sequencing actions, or generating novel solutions. The review’s I5 defines problem solving as involving evaluation/planning/sequencing operations to reach a goal; this study focuses on memory retrieval of learned facts and rehearsal effects, not on solving new or structured problems. Therefore I5 is not met, and the study should be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=42) using mental arithmetic (multiplication and subtraction), which constitutes a goal-directed, rule-based problem-solving task. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and cluster/FWE thresholds, and describes BOLD acquisition and voxelwise results in tables/figures. ROI analyses are also present but do not replace the whole-brain results. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of inductive logical reasoning (syllogisms) in healthy adults, which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (logical operations to reach a conclusion). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, stereotactic MNI coordinates for activations, and BOLD results; coordinates and voxelwise results are presented in tables/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines mental arithmetic problems that require goal-directed calculation and procedural operations (carrying/borrowing), meeting the review definition of problem solving. It used a whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adult participants (n=16). Data were normalized to MNI305 stereotactic space and analyzed with voxelwise thresholds (SPM99), and BOLD fMRI was used, satisfying stereotactic coordinate reporting and BOLD criteria. Voxelwise results are reported in group analyses and supported by individual subject maps, consistent with allowance for coordinates in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, includes healthy-group task effects, and is not limited to ROIs or only between-group clinical comparisons. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of landmark/order memory for familiar routes (landmark order-judgment match–mismatch). It meets I6 (group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). However, it does not meet I5: the task is retrieval/recognition of learned landmark sequences and match–mismatch judgments, not a problem-solving paradigm as defined (goal-directed novel problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a solution). Additionally, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI peak coordinates in the excerpt, so I7 is not demonstrably met from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failure to satisfy the core problem-solving inclusion criterion (I5) and for lack of clear reporting of stereotactic coordinates (I7).

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study of deductive/ logical reasoning (syllogistic problem solving) in healthy adults (n=14). The task meets the review’s problem-solving definition (logical rule-based evaluation to arrive at correct conclusions), satisfying I5. The study used whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates after normalization to an MNI template (I7), and reports BOLD activation results (I8). Voxelwise results and peak coordinates are reported in the text (and implied tables/figures), satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group patient comparison, and is an original empirical report). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates solving arithmetic problems (multiplication and division). The tasks meet the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed calculation, planning/sequence of operations within an algebraic framework). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM2, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for task-related activations, and uses BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are reported and ROI analyses are supplementary. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based PET study of mental calculation (abacus-based contiguous addition), which meets the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed arithmetic operations following rule sets). It reports whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adult participants (abacus experts and non-experts) using SPM2, with rCBF PET data (15O-water). Results are presented in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space with voxelwise activation maps/tables and between- and within-group contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of task design and coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects). Therefore the study satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included.

The fMRI study does not meet the required definition of a problem-solving task for the meta-analysis. Although participants performed navigation learning (which involves planning) during training, the neuroimaging acquisition and reported task effects are from a retrieval/classification task (identifying which maze a landmark belonged to), not an active problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning or rule-based solution operations during scanning. The full text is complete and reports whole-brain exploratory group analyses (with MNI coordinates) and BOLD results, but the critical inclusion criterion I5 (task-based fMRI/PET of a problem-solving task as defined) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain analysis with group-level effects), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (qualifying voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task during fMRI is retrieval/classification, not problem-solving). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that investigates arithmetic (multiplication verification) and magnitude judgment. The multiplication verification task meets the review’s problem-solving definition: it has a clear goal, requires applying arithmetic rules/operations and evaluating candidate answers (produce-compare strategy). The study reports whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses in healthy adults, provides stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates for task-related activations, and uses BOLD fMRI (EPI) measures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of deductive/transitive inference (acoustic reasoning) in healthy adult participants (12 right-handed males), which operationalizes a problem-solving task (logical/transitive inference—goal to determine spatial relation via logical integration). The study performed whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM5 normalization and cluster-level inference) and reports task-related activations across the brain (detailed cluster results described and thresholds given). The methods indicate normalization to standard stereotactic space and typical reporting of voxelwise cluster peaks; task BOLD contrasts and resulting cluster-level results are described, consistent with reporting stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a mental calculation task (subtractions/additions/multiplications) that meets the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed operations following rules to reach correct solutions). The study reports whole-brain random effects analyses with voxelwise results and peak coordinates in standardized space (MNI), presents BOLD fMRI contrasts (calculation vs control), and provides group-level effects. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study includes a task that meets the review’s definition of problem solving (a deductive logic localizer where participants judged validity of arguments), reports group-level whole-brain analyses, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach-normalized) in tables and text. The paper contains full methods, results (including whole-brain and ROI analyses derived from the logic localizer), and discussion in healthy adult participants. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates; however, the experimental task is mental rotation/discrimination (judging whether two images are identical or mirror images), which is a visuospatial imagery/discrimination task rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined in I5 (involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or executing operations within a rule set to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore it does not meet I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none ([])

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ACC and lPFC) analyses and percent signal-change results rather than whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps or stereotactic coordinate tables of activation peaks. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of a problem-solving task in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no evidence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (no task-related activation peaks reported as stereotactic coordinates in results/tables—ROI center coordinates are provided but not whole-brain activation coordinates), I9 (no indication that voxelwise results are available in tables/figures/supplement). Exclusion criterion met: E3 (reports only ROI results). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided). Inclusion criteria met based on abstract: I5 (task-based fMRI of a matrix/fluid reasoning problem-solving task) and I8 (reports BOLD signal results). Inclusion criteria that cannot be confirmed due to missing full text: I6 (unclear if sample is healthy adults and that at least one whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults is reported despite mention of mixed-effects), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported in the abstract), and I9 (cannot verify voxelwise coordinate tables/figures/supplementary). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract. Because key inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I9) cannot be verified and the full text is incomplete, I exclude the study pending full-text availability.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the Raven's Progressive Matrices (a well-established problem-solving/fluid-reasoning task), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=79). Whole-brain analyses were performed (group ICA, within-subject ANOVA) with group-level effects reported. The study uses BOLD fMRI. Stereotactic locations and cluster peaks are indicated (MNI standard space is referenced and Supplementary Table I is described as providing voxel locations for RPM–rest contrasts), satisfying coordinate reporting and acceptable placement in supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental coordinate tables are referenced. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of linear-order (transitive) reasoning—a problem-solving/relational-inference task meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. It reports whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analyses (including maps for all participants and within non-depressed participants), uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (cluster peaks reported). Voxelwise results are reported and supplementary tables are referenced. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results with peak coordinates (MNI) and group-level analyses, but the experimental paradigm is spatial working memory and perspective-taking (allocentric vs egocentric recall), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no explicit goal-directed problem to be solved, planning/sequencing of actions, or executing operations to derive a novel solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group fMRI), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), and I9 (coordinate results available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of spatial memory/navigation (pointing to a start location after traversing virtual mazes). It does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5): the authors explicitly state “As only one direction was possible at each turn, no route planning was required,” indicating no requirement for planning/sequencing or other critical problem-solving operations. The study does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported, e.g., XYZ = -34 -34 -6), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results available in supplementary material). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Thus the paper must be excluded because it fails I5 (problem-solving task).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20) that investigates logical reasoning/disjunction-elimination embedded in narratives — participants must infer implicit premises and draw conclusions, which fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical operations to arrive at a solution). The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses (GLM, one-sample t tests), includes BOLD fMRI data, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related activations and connectivity results. Voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in the text/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-healthy-group task effects).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of arithmetic (a rule-based problem-solving task) using whole-brain BOLD analyses and Talairach normalization, the participant sample for the healthy/control group is mixed adolescents and young adults (ages ~10.8–22.7, mean ~17). The meta-analysis requires group-level effects in healthy adult individuals; because the control group is not restricted to adults (many participants are minors) the study does not meet inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (problem-solving arithmetic task), I7 (data normalized to Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (results indicated in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Thus the study must be excluded due to failure to meet I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that uses arithmetic (exact and approximate calculation) tasks which constitute rule-based problem-solving (goal-directed operations to compute or estimate sums). The study reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses using SPM, provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI), and presents voxelwise results in tables/figures. Therefore it satisfies I5 (task meets problem-solving definition via algebraic/arithmetic operations), I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (results available in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/references).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using social and mechanical reasoning tasks that require goal-directed inference and problem solving (physics puzzles and false-belief/social inference questions). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (random- and fixed-effects) on 45 healthy adults, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic peak coordinates (711-2B/Talairach-space) and voxelwise results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that investigates relational reasoning—a logical problem-solving task requiring goal-directed inference and manipulation of relations (meets the review definition of problem solving). The study reports group-level, whole-brain analyses using SPM with cluster-level correction, provides stereotactic coordinates referenced to Talairach space, and uses BOLD EPI fMRI. Voxelwise/task-related activation results are described across the whole brain (conjunctions and contrasts) with coordinates and cluster descriptions. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London (a canonical planning/problem-solving paradigm that requires goal specification, planning/sequencing moves, and rule-constrained operations), satisfying the review's problem-solving task definition. The study includes healthy adult participants and reports within-group and between-group whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (second-level independent t-tests and within-group main effects), with task-related BOLD fMRI results reported in MNI stereotactic space and referenced supporting tables/figures. Voxelwise results are available in supporting information. Although the sample includes Parkinson’s patients, the paper reports healthy control group task effects and whole-brain coordinates, meeting all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical H2(15)O-PET study using the Tower of London planning task, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning, sequencing actions, rule-based solution). It includes a healthy adult control group and reports whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses (categorical and correlational), with voxelwise stereotactic coordinates reported in tables/figures (Talairach/MNI) and analyses of regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF). Voxelwise results are presented in tables and figures. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-empirical, or lack of healthy-group task effects) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a serial-arithmetic task that requires goal-directed planning, sequencing of operations, and rule-based execution—meeting the review's operational definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, presents stereotactic coordinates (Talairach), and uses BOLD fMRI measures. Results are reported in tables and figures with voxelwise contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group patient/age/gender comparison, and not non-empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of empathic reasoning about facial expressions, not a problem-solving task as defined by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results described in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the task requires selecting which of four situational sentences best matches an observed facial expression (social/emotional inference), but does not involve problem-solving as defined (goal-directed planning, sequencing operations or applying rule-based procedures to arrive at a novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it fails I5 (problem-solving task requirement).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (17 right-handed males, mean age 28) investigating multi-digit addition. The task qualifies as problem solving per the review definition (goal-directed computation, planning/sequencing of column-wise operations and execution of arithmetic rules, including carry operations). The study reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (second-level SPM analyses) and provides voxelwise stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related BOLD effects across multiple contrasts (parametric regressors: unit sum, decade sum, carry, distractor type). BOLD (fMRI) analyses are explicitly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group/disease comparison, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=28) using a maze navigation task that meets the review definition of problem solving (clear goal: reach maze end; planning/sequencing and execution of actions). The authors report group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects, contrasts across participants), BOLD fMRI methods, and state stereotactic coordinate results (coordinates/figures referenced). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that employed reasoning and episodic-memory-based reasoning tasks (meets I5), performed group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (meets I6), and reports BOLD-based fMRI results (meets I8). However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate results in either Talairach or MNI space (no coordinate tables or coordinate figures are shown in the supplied content), so inclusion criterion I7 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because not all required inclusion criteria are met (missing I7).

Full text reports a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in adult participants (healthy controls and adults with developmental dyscalculia) performing semantic/quantity and perceptual (colour) decision tasks. The number and object semantic tasks involve goal-directed, rule-based operations (select larger/smaller number or categorize by semantic rules), which fit the review’s definition of problem-solving as executing semantic/ rule-constrained operations to arrive at correct solutions. The study includes group-level whole-brain SPM analyses with appropriate covariates and multiple comparison correction, reports MNI stereotactic coordinates for activations (e.g., IPS and frontal regions), and uses BOLD fMRI. All required data for inclusion (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are present; no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in standardized (MNI) space, and provides voxelwise results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by I5. The paradigm investigates theory-of-mind/social judgment (predicting an agent's choice by inferring beliefs and desires) and manipulates abductive vs. deductive mental-state reasoning; this is social-cognitive inference rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a correct solution in a non-social problem-solving domain. No exclusion criteria are met (E3–E6). Therefore the article is excluded for failing inclusion criterion I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (WCST), which meets our problem-solving definition (goal-directed rule discovery and execution, planning/sequencing to reach correct responses). The paper includes whole-brain, group-level analyses for healthy adult controls (n=15) and reports task-related activation coordinates in standardized space (Talairach) from BOLD fMRI analyses. Results are presented in tables/figures and correlations are reported. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, lack of healthy-group task effects, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and is eligible for inclusion.

The study is a task-based whole-brain fMRI investigation in healthy adult physicians/residents performing clinical reasoning MCQs that require goal-directed problem solving (diagnosis). It reports group-level, voxelwise BOLD analyses with stereotactic Talairach coordinates and provides coordinate results in tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of clinical reasoning (answering vignette-based MCQs), which constitutes a problem-solving task (goal: determine diagnosis; requires evaluation, planning/selection and execution to arrive at a correct answer). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with group-level effects (experts vs novices), uses BOLD fMRI (EPI), and reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (figures/tables). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This PET study uses FDG to measure baseline glucose metabolism and metabolic changes during a cognitive (numerical calculations) task in healthy adults (n=21). It meets I5 (numerical calculations are algebraic/problem-solving operations), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise SPM group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported for clusters), and I9 (voxelwise results presented in figures/tables). However, it does not report BOLD or regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) measures; FDG-PET measures glucose metabolism (CMRglc), not BOLD or rCBF, so inclusion criterion I8 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I8).

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adults using a mental arithmetic task that meets the definition of problem-solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations within a rule set). It reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with group-level effects in healthy adults, provides stereotactic coordinates for rCBF increases, and reports regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) PET results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria apply.

Although this task-based fMRI study examines problem-solving tasks (calendrical calculation and division) in a healthy adult and reports MNI-normalized BOLD results and connectivity/voxelwise analyses, it is a single-subject (n=1) study and does not provide group-level whole-brain effects. Inclusion criterion I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adult individuals) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of moral reasoning (personal/impersonal moral dilemmas) in healthy adults and patients with bvFTD. It meets several methodological inclusion criteria (I6: includes whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults; I7: reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space; I8: reports BOLD task-related analyses; I9: voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in main text/tables/supplement). However, it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem‑solving task (I5): the moral reasoning paradigm involves ethical deliberation about dilemmas, not goal-directed problem solving characterized by planning/sequencing operations within a rule-based framework to arrive at a correct solution. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=30) investigating logical problem-solving (transitive reasoning/set-inclusion and linear relations), which fits the definition of problem solving (logical rules/inference). Group-level whole-brain analyses and localizer contrasts were conducted using SPM8, with results reported in MNI stereotaxic space (coordinates provided). The paper reports BOLD analyses and voxelwise results (including small-volume corrected voxelwise findings in left RLPFC) and provides coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a problem-solving task (trial-and-error search with exploration/exploitation). It reports whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses, BOLD results, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. The task meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed search, evaluation, planning/execution to find correct stimulus). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of numerical perception/processing (nonsymbolic and symbolic numerosity, summation and number-selective coding, connectivity). It includes healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates. However, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to reach a solution). The tasks are perceptual/recognition and connectivity paradigms (dot displays, digit recognition/matching), not problem-solving across domains. Therefore, exclude.

Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3-E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of deductive reasoning (logical and linguistic inference) in healthy adult participants. The inference tasks involve evaluating validity (goal-directed logical problem solving), fitting the review's definition of problem solving using logical rules. The study reports group-level whole-brain mixed-effects analyses with BOLD contrast maps, stereotactic (MNI) normalization, and voxelwise results (tables and SI). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task: logical deduction), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in standardized space), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/SI). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations, so it fails inclusion criterion I7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the imagined navigation task involves goal-directed route planning and planning sequences to reach a destination), I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses and group-average maps are reported), and I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI was used and analyzed). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no stereotactic coordinates for task activations are provided in the supplied full text). The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the provided content.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of a problem-solving task (Chinese chess checkmate problems). The task has a clear goal (find a checkmate), requires planning/sequencing moves and rule-based operations, matching the review’s problem-solving definition. Participants are healthy adult groups (grandmasters/masters and novices). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses with random-effects group-level one-sample and two-sample t-tests, uses BOLD fMRI (task-based contrasts), and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and voxelwise (AlphaSim-corrected) maps. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to disease/age/gender group comparisons, include within-group healthy task effects, and it is empirical primary research. The full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation of moral reasoning comparing ASD patients and healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (reports whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (task-related BOLD fMRI results), I9 (voxelwise results are presented in tables/figures/supplement). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task is moral decision-making/dilemma evaluation rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review, which requires goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing operations within defined rule sets—semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical, etc.). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task per the review’s I5 definition.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation using the Tower of London — a well-established problem-solving/executive planning task (meets I5). It includes a healthy adult control group and reports group-level whole-brain analyses using SPM99 random-effects models (meets I6). Results are reported in MNI stereotactic space with tables/figures of activation peaks (meets I7 and I9). The modality is BOLD fMRI (meets I8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided article is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not purely between-group without healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I5: it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined. The experimental tasks are perceptual spatial judgments (allocentric vs. egocentric left/right decisions and luminance discrimination) rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing, or executing operations to discover a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because the study investigates autobiographical memory and self-reflection (remembering content vs reflecting on meaning) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the meta-analysis (I5 not met). The study does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic/MNI coordinates), I8 (task-related BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a mental-arithmetic task that requires goal-directed operations (repeated subtraction) and thus meets the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM99, presents BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (e.g., x=−34,y=−42,z=42) with tables/figures, and includes BOLD analyses and functional connectivity. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental (multidigit) addition in healthy adult bilinguals. The arithmetic tasks require goal-directed operations, planning/sequence operations (columnwise addition or rounding estimation), and execution under rule-based frameworks, fitting the review’s definition of problem solving. Whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM5; results are reported in MNI space with coordinates (supplementary tables/figures) and BOLD-based contrasts (task > baseline). The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient/group-contrast-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I9 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study of problem solving (Tower of Hanoi variant) in healthy adult participants (N=8) that explicitly operationalizes planning/problem solving. The analysis used voxel-wise, between-subject (group-level) regressions across brain voxels, reporting BOLD results and presenting stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) in Table 1. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster thresholding and significance levels) and provides methods, results, and discussion in full. All specified inclusion criteria are met (I5: problem-solving task; I6: group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults; I7: stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach space; I8: BOLD analysis; I9: voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a multiplication verification task that requires goal-directed calculation, sequencing and execution of arithmetic operations (meets I5). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses in Talairach space with cluster-level correction and provides stereotactic/ROI coordinates (meets I6 and I7). It uses BOLD fMRI (meets I8) and voxelwise results are available in tables/figures (meets I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study is not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Although this study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in MNI space (meeting I6, I7, I8, I9), it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in the review protocol. The target task is the Alternate Uses Task (AUT), a divergent thinking/creativity fluency task that asks participants to generate uses for objects rather than to identify or execute rule-based operations to reach a correct or more appropriate solution (the study explicitly treats AUT as a creativity/divergent-thinking measure). Therefore Inclusion Criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task per protocol definition) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study reports a task (virtual Morris Water Task) that meets the review's problem-solving definition: subjects have a clear goal (find the platform) and must plan and execute navigation/search strategies to reach it. It uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain analyses (ICA and GLM) and reports group-level effects including healthy adult controls. Results are presented in standardized MNI space and include BOLD signal analyses and voxelwise results (ICA components, GLM contrasts, VBM associations), satisfying reporting requirements. The full-text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI results, is empirical with original human data, and includes healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included.

This is a patient fMRI case study of number processing after left ventral occipito-temporal damage. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (study includes whole-brain second-level analyses with a healthy control group), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Primary inclusion criterion not met: I5. The tasks are semantic/magnitude comparisons (quantity: larger/smaller; category: summer/winter; and a color-perceptual task) and do not constitute the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed multi-step planning, sequencing, critical evaluation or execution toward a novel solution). The paper’s focus is on compensatory neural mechanisms in a stroke patient rather than investigating problem-solving across domains in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This study does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review. It reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain group analyses (I6) and BOLD measures (I8). However, the tasks used are a false-belief (Theory of Mind) paradigm and a Go/No-go inhibitory control task, which do not meet the review's problem-solving definition (I5 not met). The provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinates in the excerpt (I7 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply based on the provided content. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I5 (and I7 is not clearly satisfied in the provided text).

Full text is complete. This is an fMRI study of allocentric social hierarchy and alliance judgements in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the tasks are social-status and alliance judgments/forced-choice perceptual decisions rather than goal-directed problem-solving tasks as defined (planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a solution across domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of problem-solving across domains and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (a rule-based problem-solving task) in healthy adults. It includes group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses (N=16 fMRI participants) with MNI-normalized stereotactic coordinates reported, BOLD-based analyses, and voxelwise/parametric results presented in figures and peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of conditional reasoning (Wason selection-style rule-broken task) in 24 healthy adults, employing whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects, FWE/FDR corrections) and reporting region-level activations normalized to MNI space. The task requires applying logical/rule-based operations to determine rule violations, fitting the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed, rule-based evaluation/planning to reach correct judgments). BOLD fMRI analyses are reported. The main text references voxelwise activation results (BA labels and cluster-level statistics) and indicates normalization to MNI and use of standard stereotactic reporting, consistent with availability of coordinates in tables/figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-healthy groups only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of Theory of Mind (true/false belief reasoning), not a problem-solving task as defined by I5. While the paper meets imaging-related criteria (whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adults, reports BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates), the experimental paradigm focuses on social mental-state attribution (belief-based behaviour attribution) rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach an unknown solution. Therefore I5 is not satisfied, so the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London variant) in healthy adults that operationalizes problem solving (goal state, planning/evaluation and execution). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (random-effects), uses BOLD fMRI, normalizes into MNI space and provides stereotactic coordinates and tables/figures of activations. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=24 analyzed). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only group comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, not a review). Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion, references present). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using the Wason selection task (logical/problem-solving task requiring identification of violations and rule-based reasoning). It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and cluster results, and describes BOLD imaging methods and results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based problem-solving fMRI studies (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses a task-based fMRI Tower of London planning paradigm that fulfills the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses for adult participants (including separate main-effect maps for OCS low scoring twins, i.e., healthy adults). Results are reported as voxelwise BOLD effects with MNI stereotactic coordinates presented in tables and figures. Voxelwise whole-brain analyses (including task vs baseline and task-load contrasts) are explicitly described and thresholding/cluster criteria provided. Although the sample comprises twins discordant for obsessive–compulsive symptoms (with a few meeting OCD criteria), the paper provides healthy-group task effects and whole-brain coordinate results, meeting inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning/problem-solving paradigm (meets I5). It includes healthy adult control participants and reports group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses comparing controls and HD groups (meets I6). Analyses are BOLD-based (meets I8). Data were spatially normalized to MNI space, a seed coordinate in MNI is reported (MNI −4/54/−8), and the manuscript describes voxelwise cluster results and refers to cluster/figure information (satisfies I7 and I9 given that stereotactic results are presented in MNI space and cluster results are indicated in the paper/figures). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical).

This PET study reports a task-based investigation of semantic decision-making (and syllable decisions) that the authors frame and interpret as involving complex/‘verbal problem-solving’ and relational semantic reasoning. It meets imaging and reporting requirements: healthy adult sample (n=19), group-level whole-brain PET (rCBF) analyses using SPM99, stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space, and voxelwise results presented in figures/tables. The semantic task entails goal-directed selection among alternatives and controlled semantic elaboration (consistent with the review’s definition of problem solving, including semantic problem-solving). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, coordinates) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. The study does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task is moral decision-making (everyday moral conflicts), not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations within a rule set to arrive at a solution). The paper does meet other technical criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in standardized stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI reported), and I9 (voxelwise results/tables and figures presented). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I5 (does not investigate problem-solving as defined).

This is a whole-brain, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD effects with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates; however, the experimental task is sentence reading to probe referential/semantic language processing rather than an explicit, goal-directed problem-solving task as defined by the review. Specifically: (a) No exclusion criteria were met (none of E3–E6 apply). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise results available in text/tables/figures). (c) Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task is language comprehension/pronoun resolution during passive reading and was not designed or instructed as a goal-directed problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing/execution to reach a solution according to the review’s definition). Therefore the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that operationalises problem solving as probabilistic/inductive reasoning (constructing competing hypotheses and selecting the best fit), which fits the review's problem-solving definition. The paper reports a group-level whole-brain (fixed-effects) voxelwise analysis, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI→Talairach) of activation peaks, and reports BOLD (fMRI) results.
