The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Although the sample is small and analyses are fixed-effects (not random-effects), the study nonetheless meets the stated inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI experiment in healthy adults that explicitly implemented a goal-directed problem-solving simulation task (participants imagined solving problems and formulating plans), satisfying the review's problem-solving definition. It reports whole-brain, group-level (random-effects) GLM analyses and seed PLS functional connectivity, with stereotactic MNI coordinates provided for activations (e.g., PCC, DLPFC). Voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in the main text and supplementary materials. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that includes a problem-solving/planning paradigm (Tower of London) meeting the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing). The study performed group-level whole-brain GLM analyses (Test and Repetition samples) with SPM, normalized to MNI space, and reports lists of significant clusters (coordinates) for task contrasts (planning vs baseline). BOLD EPI fMRI was the modality used. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and provides adequate detail for inclusion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Beauty Contest game, which requires a clear goal (win the prize) and rule-based strategic reasoning/planning (iterated best-reply, mental calculation, and action selection) consistent with the review's definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random effects analyses in 20 healthy adults, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activations (e.g., mPFC, TPJ), and uses BOLD fMRI measures. Coordinates and contrasts are reported in the main text and supplementary materials. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes within-healthy-group task effects). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical PET study with 41 healthy adults performing two problem-solving/abstract reasoning tasks (WCST and Raven’s Progressive Matrices), which meet the review’s problem-solving definition. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise SPM analyses (task minus control), provides group-level effects in healthy adults, and reports regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) results with stereotactic normalization to Talairach space and tabulated local maxima/coordinates in tables and figures. Voxelwise results and across-task comparisons are presented. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects beyond age comparisons). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study of reasoning in healthy adults that explicitly requires subjects to deduce and apply a sequencing rule (i.e., problem-solving involving goal-directed planning/sequencing). The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (FDR-corrected) in normalized stereotactic space (MNI305), provides stereotactic results/coordinates (figures/tables referenced), and uses BOLD fMRI. Participants are healthy adults (n=19). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not clinical-group comparisons only, includes within-healthy-group task effects, and is empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a mental calculation (multiplication) task that constitutes an algebraic/problem-solving task. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (task vs rest), provides BOLD fMRI results, and lists peak activation coordinates in MNI space (e.g., left intraparietal sulcus x = −34, y = −50, z = 48). Voxelwise results and supplementary data are indicated. Sample consists of healthy adult participants. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates. However, the experimental tasks are nonsymbolic numerical, spatial orientation, and color discriminations (magnitude/comparison and perceptual decision tasks), not problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (i.e., requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at novel solutions). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults examining relational reasoning/transitive inference, which constitutes a logical problem-solving task (deriving comparative relations and planning/sequence operations to infer novel relations). The study performed whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analyses (FLAME), reports stereotactic peak coordinates in MNI space, and reports BOLD results. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical human data).

The study is task-based fMRI in healthy adults and tests goal-direction/navigation judgments which involve planning/simulation (meets I5). It reports whole-brain MVPA/searchlight group analyses (meets I6) and uses BOLD fMRI (meets I8). The manuscript indicates voxelwise results available in figures/supplement (meets I9). However, the provided full text does not report task-related stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach or MNI space (I7 not demonstrated in the content supplied). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, patient-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Because I7 is required and cannot be verified from the provided text, the study must be excluded. Full text appears otherwise complete in results/discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review. It uses a color-word Stroop inhibitory control task to probe error processing and insight in cocaine use disorder, not tasks requiring goal-directed problem identification, planning/sequencing, and solution generation across domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (performs whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy control participants), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does NOT study a problem-solving task per the review definition). Exclusion criteria met: none (does not meet E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on problem-solving in healthy adults.

This study uses task-based fMRI (BOLD) to examine cognitive planning/problem solving with the Tower of London paradigm (meets I5). Analysis includes whole-brain, voxelwise group-level effects using SPM5 with normalization to MNI space and reported cluster peak coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8). Voxelwise results and coordinate data are reported in tables/figures referenced in the text (meets I9). Participants are healthy adult monozygotic twins drawn from a population register (concordant-low groups provide healthy adult task effects); although a small number had clinical OCD, the study reports whole-brain task effects and group contrasts relevant to healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not solely disease/age/gender comparisons, includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results in standardized stereotactic space, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The experimental tasks assess theory-of-mind (false belief) and counterfactual reasoning about social vignettes, focusing on mentalizing, semantic processing and executive control. These tasks require inference and simulation but do not involve a goal-directed problem with planning/sequencing actions to reach a solution in the sense of the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (I5). All other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes the Tower of London (planning/problem-solving) task, which meets the definition of problem-solving (goal-directed planning and sequencing to reach a solution). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and reports BOLD fMRI results (with coordinates in main text and supplementary material). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adult participants (graduate students) using a mental rotation task that requires goal-directed transformation operations to determine sameness — consistent with the review's definition of problem solving. It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (ANOVA) and task-related BOLD effects (Compare vs Control), uses Talairach stereotactic space (coordinates and ROI centers reported), and provides voxelwise/cluster results in figures/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5-I9) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text is complete and the study is task-based fMRI using the False-Belief (theory-of-mind) Localizer, with whole-brain group analyses in large healthy reference samples, reported stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD analyses. However, the experimental task does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5): false-belief reasoning/toM manipulates mental-state inference rather than a goal-directed problem-solving process requiring planning/sequencing operations within a formal rule set (semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical) to arrive at a solution. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Excluded because the task is semantic truth/false verification rather than a goal-directed, novel problem-solving task as defined in I5. Although authors interpret false-item processing as involving reasoning, the paradigm assesses recognition/verification of stored knowledge rather than planning/sequencing or generating novel solutions. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported/used with anatomical localization), I8 (BOLD fMRI reported), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (does not clearly operationalize a problem-solving task as defined). No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The task in this study is a numerical magnitude comparison (size-congruity/number-Stroop), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning, sequencing actions or generating novel solutions). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (data transformed to Talairach space and results indicated as reported in tables/figures), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level analyses that report stereotactic coordinates (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied). However, the task used (mental rotation) is a visuospatial transformation task rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical frameworks). Therefore I5 is not met and the study does not address the review's problem-solving objective. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that required active problem solving (algebra equation generation), satisfying the problem-solving definition. The study reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (voxel-wise ANOVAs, Monte-Carlo cluster thresholding) and provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space for task-related effects. It uses BOLD fMRI and reports task-related increases; voxelwise results are described and reported in tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are applicable.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Wason card selection task (a conditional/logical reasoning problem-solving paradigm). It reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise results) in healthy adults, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and reports BOLD fMRI activation results. The behavioral task fits the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed conditional reasoning using logical rules). The paper also presents both ROI and whole-brain results, and not ROI-only. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a whole-brain task-based fMRI (BOLD) random-effects group analysis reporting MNI coordinates and tables/figures, but the experimental task investigates belief reasoning / theory of mind (true vs false belief) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-oriented planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain group-level effects with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and BOLD analyses (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task is a reinforcement-learning/win-stay radial-arm maze designed to probe stimulus–response (S–R) learning and habit formation. The task does not involve the type of problem-solving as defined in the review (i.e., explicit identification/evaluation of a problem, planning or sequencing actions using rule-based operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task as defined) is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study does not investigate problem-solving as defined in I5. Its tasks are navigation/object-location memory and scene/object perception (spatial vs non-spatial) rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution. The paper is task-based fMRI in healthy adults, includes whole-brain analyses, reports MNI coordinates, and BOLD results. Thus it satisfies I6, I7, I8, and I9 but fails I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates (MNI). However, the experimental paradigm investigates creative generation and evaluation during book-cover illustration design — an open-ended creative task — rather than an explicit problem-solving task as defined by the review (a goal-directed task requiring planning/sequence of operations within a rule set to arrive at a correct or specific solution). The manuscript does not frame the task as solving a defined problem with a correct/target solution or apply explicit task constraints characteristic of typical problem-solving paradigms. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. All other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI experiment in healthy adults performing a single-trial rule induction/hypothesis-testing task that involves goal-directed rule discovery and updating. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task involves rule-based hypothesis testing/problem-solving processes), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adult participants), and I8 (BOLD fMRI reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space; no coordinate tables or coordinate listings are present in the supplied content). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present) but the absence of explicit stereotactic coordinates in the provided document prevents meeting all required inclusion criteria, so the study is excluded for I7 not being satisfied.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in the meta-analysis objective. It is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study of Theory of Mind (ToM) using animated shapes and contrasts ToM versus random motion; the task does not involve goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations, or rule-based solution execution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (includes whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported/tabled). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (does NOT study a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3, E4, E5, or E6). Full text appears complete. Because I5 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Although it uses task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic coordinates (meeting I6, I7, I8, and I9), the experimental paradigm is route learning/spatial navigation and memory (encoding and retrieval of temporo-spatial landmark associations), not a domain-general problem-solving task as defined by I5 (i.e., a goal-directed need to figure out a method, involving critical evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions or rule-based operations to reach a novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of reasoning/problem-solving (Transitive Inference and Letter Series tasks) in healthy adult participants. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analyses (FLAME1+2) with cluster-based correction, registration to MNI space, and presentation of cluster locations/statistics (figures and tables), indicating voxelwise stereotactic results are available. It also reports BOLD task-related activation changes and between-group (training vs control) effects. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results with stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The experimental tasks are number-line estimation and brightness estimation (mapping magnitudes to spatial positions), which are estimation/psychophysical tasks rather than goal-directed problem-solving requiring planning, sequencing, or execution of operations to reach an unknown solution. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables), so exclusion is based on ineligible task content rather than incomplete reporting or other exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning and sequencing of moves). The study includes healthy adult control subjects and reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (main effects in controls and group interactions). Results are reported as BOLD signal changes and presented with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach space) in tables/figures. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a problem-solving task (pyramid math problems) that requires goal-directed planning and algorithm execution/modification. The study reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise exploratory analyses (Pre-Regular vs Post-Exception contrast) with identified regions and coordinates, and predefined region analyses reported in Talairach space. Imaging methods (EPI, TR/TE, preprocessing) and results (voxel clusters, t-values, coordinates, figures/tables) are reported. There is clear evidence of task-related BOLD increases and whole-brain effects predicting learning. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This task-based fMRI study includes the Tower of London planning task, which meets the definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning and sequencing). It reports BOLD-based fMRI analyses, performs whole-brain SPM group-level analyses normalized to MNI space (with whole-brain FDR correction and rendered statistical parametric maps), and includes healthy adult control participants with group-level task effects and patient-control comparisons. Voxelwise/whole-brain results are presented as statistical maps (figures) and ROI and region-level coordinates are provided (e.g., MNI coordinates for ROIs), satisfying the requirement that stereotactic/MNI-referenced task-related activations are reported or available. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experiment is a theory-of-mind (belief–desire reasoning) task that probes social cognition and executive control to predict an agent's action, rather than a task framed as goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution per the meta-analysis definition. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results/figures are reported or indicated). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task as defined), I7 (the provided full text does not explicitly list stereotactic coordinate tables in standardized space within the excerpt). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study does not meet the meta-analysis task definition of problem solving (I5). The experimental task is spatial navigation and memory (judgment of relative direction and pointing), which tests allocentric spatial representation and retrieval rather than goal-directed problem-solving involving planning, sequencing, or applying rule-based operations across domains. The study does satisfy whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6) and reports BOLD analyses (I8). However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate results (Talairach/MNI) in the included content, so I7 cannot be confirmed from the supplied document. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the provided content.

This is a methods/VR-stimulus development paper reporting a spatial navigation/memory task (explore/memorize a virtual city) in 4 healthy adults with BOLD fMRI and group-level (fixed-effect) whole-brain analyses. It does not investigate or operationalize a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met — the paradigm is navigation/memory, not goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution). The paper does report BOLD analyses and group-level whole-brain results (I6 and I8 met), but stereotactic coordinate tables are not clearly provided in the supplied text (I7 not clearly met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I5 (and lacking clear evidence for I7).

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in healthy adults with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and provides coordinate tables/figures, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5). The tasks are passive listening, parity judgments, and magnitude comparisons—simple semantic/decision tasks that do not require goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a novel or rule-based solution. Thus I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses a task-based fMRI paradigm (BOLD) in healthy adult participants performing a stepwise category induction task that requires a clear goal (identify the invariant/target category) and iterative hypothesis testing, evaluation, and elimination of alternatives — processes consistent with problem-solving as defined in I5. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates for activations (e.g., x=-42,y=26,z=37 and others) consistent with Talairach/MNI reporting (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI analyses (I8). Voxelwise/task-related results and PPI coordinates are described in the text and tables (acceptable per I9). Participants were healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experimental tasks are reality evaluation (judging pictures as real vs. unreal) and recognition memory, which involve perception, context appraisal and relational reasoning but are not defined as goal-directed problem-solving requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution. Furthermore, the reported neuroimaging results focus on between-group comparisons (patients vs. controls) and group-difference coordinates rather than clearly reporting healthy-group within-task activation maps; thus it effectively lacks a standalone healthy-group task effect needed for inclusion and matches exclusion E5. The paper does, however, report whole-brain BOLD fMRI analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=13) that reports whole-brain, group-level analyses and BOLD results. The cognitive task includes serial subtraction (arithmetic) performed as part of a divided-attention paradigm; arithmetic/problem-solving operations fit the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed operations within an algebraic/arithmetic rule set). Images were transformed to Talairach space and group voxelwise activation (Table 2, Fig. 1) is reported, satisfying stereotactic coordinate reporting. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

The study reports an event-related whole-brain fMRI experiment in healthy adult humans (n=16) in which participants infer and apply novel syntactic rules to judge strings (sample block + probe block). This task requires establishing a goal (identify correct strings), inferring rules from examples, and executing rule-based decisions—meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. The paper reports group-level random-effects analyses, voxelwise BOLD results with MNI coordinates, and whole-brain FDR-corrected statistics. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines quantitative (geometrical) reasoning requiring participants to compare perimeters (goal-directed evaluation and application of geometric rules), which fits the review’s definition of problem-solving. The study reports group-level whole-brain BOLD fMRI analyses (1.5 T BOLD, SPM2), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for activation peaks, and presents voxelwise results across conditions. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study of logical reasoning (syllogisms) in healthy adults that fits the review's problem-solving definition—participants must determine whether conclusions follow from premises (logical rule-based problem solving). It reports group-level, whole-brain BOLD analyses using SPM with spatial normalization to the MNI template and voxelwise stereotactic coordinates (e.g., MNI coords provided). Behavioral task, methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in the text, and analyses are not limited to ROIs. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only between-group comparisons, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task (a problem-solving paradigm). It reports whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses (planning minus subtracting contrast) in healthy older adults, with BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for significant clusters (e.g., left SPC [−36 −56 52]) and FWE-corrected statistics. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full. No ROI-only reporting or exclusionary features are present. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for a whole-brain, task-based fMRI study of problem-solving in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of spatial memory, mental imagery, and viewpoint transformations (JRD, ROT, REF). It meets inclusion criteria I6 (group-level whole-brain random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (Talairach normalization and stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures). However it does NOT meet I5: the tasks are spatial memory/imagery and perspective-taking judgments, not problem-solving tasks as defined (goal-directed critical thinking/planning/sequencing to derive novel solutions within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical or similar rule-based frameworks). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task requirement).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=32) that used a two-digit arithmetic verification task requiring procedural calculation and judgment—meeting the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed calculation using rule-based operations). The study reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (SPM5; voxel-wise t-statistics, p<0.001) and BOLD fMRI acquisition. The manuscript indicates voxelwise cluster results and refers to figures/tables for activation loci (conjunction, direct, and interaction contrasts), consistent with stereotactic reporting conventions (coordinates implied in results/tables/figures). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore I5, I6, I8 and I9 are satisfied, and I7 is considered satisfied based on the main text indicating voxelwise stereotactic results available in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes a calculation (subtraction) task meeting the review's problem-solving definition, it does not satisfy the requirement for a whole-brain group-level analysis. Imaging acquisition used only 18 axial slices “covering the parietal lobe and the majority of the prefrontal cortex, excluding the orbitofrontal sector,” indicating incomplete whole-brain coverage. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (calculation/subtraction is a rule-based problem-solving task), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise/group results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis due to limited slice coverage). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires whole-brain analyses.

Although the full text is complete and reports a whole-brain, task-based fMRI BOLD study in healthy adults with stereotactic coordinates, the experimental task assesses decision-making under risk (choosing between dice arrangements with known probabilities and incentives) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (i.e., having a goal requiring figuring out a way to reach it via critical thinking, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Thus: inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is decision-making under risk, not a domain-general problem-solving task as defined). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of two-digit mental addition in healthy adult participants, which meets the review's definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed arithmetic operations requiring rule-based computation). It reports group-level whole-brain SPM analyses with BOLD contrasts and provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I9. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This task (PASAT) requires goal-directed arithmetic operations—maintaining and manipulating sequential numbers and applying addition rules under time constraints—meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults (N=15) with group-level (second-level) whole-brain analyses (I6). fMRI BOLD methods and analyses are reported throughout (I8). The paper describes normalization to MNI space and SPM localization procedures and reports activations localized to specific brain regions (lobule VII, prefrontal areas), consistent with reporting stereotactic results in standardized space (I7); voxelwise results are described in figures/tables as implied by the methods/results (I9). The full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This task-based fMRI study employs algebraic/arithmetic operations (complex vs. simple equations) that meet the review's operational definition of problem solving (goal-directed, rule-based arithmetic evaluation/execution). It reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses in healthy adult participants (n=17), transformed into Talairach space with ROI peak coordinates and cluster sizes provided, and uses BOLD fMRI. Task-related activations (increases and decreases) are reported with timing and stereotactic localization. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

The study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5 not met). It reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults and uses BOLD fMRI and group-level analyses, but the tasks are numerical comparison/size-congruity (numerical cognition), not problem-solving (planning/sequencing/critical thinking to reach a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met / not clearly met: I5 (task is not problem solving), I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting not clearly provided in extract), I9 (coordinate reporting in tables/figures/supplementary not clearly confirmed). No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., ROI-only or patient-group only contrasts). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study used the Paced Visual Serial Addition Test (PVSAT), a working memory/processing-speed task, rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel solution). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. It does meet I6 (includes healthy adult group-level whole-brain analyses), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/supplementary). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of problem solving (compound remote associates) in healthy adult participants (I5 satisfied). It reports group-level whole-brain analyses in a healthy adult sample (n=27 for fMRI) with stereotactic normalization to Talairach space and voxelwise results (coordinates provided, e.g., −2, 42, 22) (I6, I7 satisfied). The study uses BOLD fMRI (I8 satisfied) and provides voxelwise/ROI results in tables and figures (acceptable reporting per I9). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the study used EEG with sLORETA source reconstruction rather than task-based fMRI or PET, and it does not report any BOLD or rCBF measures required by inclusion criterion I8. Additionally, the task (navigating a video game avatar) does not clearly meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain source analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach), and I9 (voxelwise-like results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is an episodic memory / narrative-insight paradigm (linking events into narratives and detecting incongruent events), not a goal-directed problem-solving task that requires planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses/searchlight reported), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI). I9 is also satisfied in that voxelwise whole-brain searchlight contrasts are described and reported. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is memory/insight, not problem-solving as defined), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space are not provided in the provided full text; coordinates may exist in supplemental materials but are not present here, so I7 cannot be confirmed). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the provided text. Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods summary, results, discussion).

This is an event-related, task-based whole-brain fMRI study of healthy adult participants performing Wason selection tasks (conditional proposition testing), which constitutes a rule-based logical problem-solving task. The paper reports group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses and BOLD (T2*-weighted EPI) results, with activation contrasts (Falsification vs BL, Non-Falsification vs BL, Falsification vs Non-Falsification, MT vs Non-Falsification, MT vs MP). Images were normalized in SPM2 and thresholded with FDR; the manuscript indicates coordinate/activation tables and supplementary materials are available online, consistent with reporting stereotactic results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient-group-only, not between-group-only, empirical human data). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult university students using problem-solving tasks (novel and old scientific innovation problems) that require identifying methods to reach a goal (meets the review’s problem-solving definition). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (NSI>OSI and reverse contrasts) with cluster-based correction, provides stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates, and BOLD fMRI results. Results are reported in the main text/tables and include voxelwise contrasts and correlations. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient-group comparisons, and is empirical). Therefore it meets I5–I9 and should be included.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level BOLD results in standardized stereotactic space. It therefore satisfies I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the experimental task is a magnitude/lateness comparison (choose larger number or later event) and semantic retrieval of known historic dates, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (i.e., it does not require setting a goal and devising/planning/executing a sequence of operations to reach a novel or nontrivial solution). The paradigm assesses number/semantic processing and sequencing/ordering judgments rather than evaluation, planning, or executing operations to solve a presented problem. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I5.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a number bisection task that requires rule-based evaluation and arithmetic operations (i.e., determining/verifying the mean), which falls under the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed evaluation and execution of operations conforming to arithmetic rules). The study reports whole-brain, random-effects (group-level) BOLD fMRI analyses, presents voxelwise stereotactic coordinates (Talairach space, e.g., BA47: 40,20,-4), and provides task-related increases across contrasts. Voxelwise results are described and presented across multiple contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group patient comparison, and is empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates learning and execution of multirule tasks (goal-directed rule application, planning/sequencing and rule-based execution). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and BOLD signal (fMRI) results (whole-brain contrasts, ROI analyses, coordinates reported). The task requires participants to form a task model and apply rule sets to achieve goals, which fits the review's operational definition of problem solving (goal, planning/sequencing, rule-based operations). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical-group comparisons only, not non-empirical). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

The study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). It investigates instruction-based learning and outcome-integration (S–R–O associations and differential vs ambiguous outcomes), which is associative/instructional learning rather than goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing or critical evaluation as defined. The full text is complete and reports whole-brain BOLD fMRI analyses in healthy adults with stereotactic coordinates and supplementary tables. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in standardized space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/supplement). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the meta-analysis definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI investigation of theory-of-mind/intentionality (mental state reasoning) using sentence-reading tasks; it does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations, or execution of operations to reach a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in standardized stereotactic space/Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based study of problem solving). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only report, no clinical-group-only contrasts, not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not address problem-solving tasks per I5.

This task-based fMRI study (healthy adults) examines inferential reasoning by exclusion, which requires subjects to infer a novel sample–comparison mapping by rejecting a trained comparison (a form of goal-directed inferential problem solving/symmetry-based reasoning). Methods report whole-brain, random-effects analyses in a healthy adult group (n=15), BOLD fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, and transformation to Talairach space; imaging contrasts (Exclusion > Baseline, S+ > Baseline) and anatomical localization are reported. The paper contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/group-only contrasts, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving/inferential task), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results placed in Talairach space/stereotactic framework), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (coordinate/results reported in figures/tables as indicated).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=14) using the Wisconsin Word Sorting Task (a lexical analog of the WCST) that requires discovering rules, planning set-shifts, and executing rule-based operations—meeting the review definition of problem-solving (goal-directed rule discovery, planning, and execution). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise BOLD analyses with normalization to MNI/Talairach space and thresholding, and presents task-related activation contrasts (semantic, rhyme, onset vs control and inter-rule contrasts) consistent with inclusion. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-empirical, between-group-only, or patient-group-only comparisons) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social vs simple truth-telling (evaluative yes/no judgments about others), not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a correct or novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results described and reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm involving goal-setting, planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not meet I5.

The study is a task-based PET experiment in healthy adults using the Montreal Card Sorting Task and reports stereotactic coordinates of task-related changes in [11C]raclopride binding. However, it does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria: (1) I6 (whole-brain analysis with group-level effects) is not met because the statistical search and inference were restricted to the striatum ("Only those peaks falling within the striatum were considered" and a striatum search volume was assumed), so a whole-brain group-level analysis is not reported; (2) I8 (reports at least one BOLD or rCBF analysis) is not met — the PET measure is raclopride binding potential (dopamine release proxy), not BOLD fMRI or rCBF. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task meets problem-solving definition: goal-directed rule inference, planning/set-shifting), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), and I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results reported in main text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that used mental arithmetic (experimental vs. control math) as the task. Mental arithmetic meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed algebraic-like operations requiring planning/manipulation). The study reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses, preprocessing and second-level mixed-effects results, and states that effect maps were transformed into MNI space and that detailed lists of activations/deactivations are available (tables/‘for detailed list see’), satisfying stereotactic-coordinate reporting. Voxelwise results were thresholded and anatomical localization performed. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study uses a task-based fMRI paradigm (Tower of London) that operationalizes problem-solving/planning (goal-directed planning, sequencing moves) consistent with the review’s problem-solving definition. Imaging used arterial spin labeling perfusion (rCBF) during task (satisfies I8). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses including a one-sample SnPM analysis in healthy controls (n=20) and reports task-related activations (planning>baseline, parametric modulation) and group comparisons (satisfies I6). The manuscript describes voxelwise cluster results and refers to tables/figures of activated regions (coordinates/tables referenced in results and supplementary), supporting stereotactic reporting (I7) and acceptable reporting in tables/figures/supplement (I9). Therefore I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results and discussion.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of moral decision-making (utilitarian vs deontological judgments) in healthy adults. While it meets several methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group analyses, MNI stereotactic coordinates reported, and BOLD fMRI analyses), the experimental task is moral dilemma judgment rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., with an explicit goal-to-solution process involving planning/sequencing operations or applying rule-based operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution). Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

While this is an event-related task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that reports BOLD results with whole-brain analyses and stereotactic normalization, the experimental task is a two-card gambling paradigm examining counterfactual thinking, reward and emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis is reported), I7 (data normalized to Talairach space and coordinates are provided for ROIs/clusters), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the task is a gambling/decision-making paradigm and does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (no evidence of a goal requiring planning/sequencing or critical thinking processes to identify/execute a solution algorithmically or to arrive at a novel/correct solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates learning and execution of algorithmic arithmetic problems (strategy vs. drill), which fits the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed, planning/sequencing operations, rule-based execution). The study used whole-brain BOLD fMRI with group-level contrasts (fixed-effects analysis across nine healthy adults), reports stereotactic coordinates transformed to Talairach space in tables, and presents voxelwise task-related activation results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient-only, empirical with healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=17) using a transitive logical-reasoning task (indeterminate/determinate trials). The task involves applying logical rules to determine validity of conclusions, fitting the review definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., 42,20,-8) and BOLD/fMRI results (I6–I8). Results and coordinates are reported in the main text and tables (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group patient comparison only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI in healthy adults performing fluid-reasoning/problem-solving tasks (matrix reasoning, paper folding, letter sets) that require goal-directed problem solving and rule-based operations (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in a healthy adult sample (N=106) (I6), uses standardized space (MNI) for preprocessing and presents coordinate-based results/tables (I7, I9), and employs BOLD EPI fMRI (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to between-group comparisons, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore include.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study but it does not meet the review’s core scope. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analyses reported), I9 (voxelwise results/tables are provided). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task is mental rotation — a visuospatial/perceptual task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review requiring goal-directed planning/sequencing/critical evaluation across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks), I6 (does not provide group-level whole-brain effects in a healthy ADULT sample exclusively — participants are male adolescents/young adults, ages ~13–21.8, and analyses focus on ASD vs matched controls rather than on healthy adult problem-solving). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3, E4, E5, E6 not applicable). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting stereotactic coordinates and BOLD effects (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task probes theory-of-mind/mental state (belief vs. desire) attribution and incongruency processing, not problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed problem identification/planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task per the review definition) is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion is based on failure to meet I5; no exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a number bisection task that requires goal-directed, rule-based operations (deciding whether the middle number is the correct mean), satisfying the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants (I6), presents stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related effects (I7), and reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8). Voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in the main text (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), the paper reports healthy-group task effects (not only between-group contrasts), and it is an empirical study. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=18) that includes an arithmetic task using Reverse Polish notation which requires goal-directed, rule-based calculation (execution of operations to arrive at a correct result), meeting the review definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (second-level SPM analyses, conjunctions), uses stereotactic normalization (MNI space) and reports voxelwise activation results and clusters (tables/figures). BOLD signal (fMRI) analyses are the main outcome. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, patient-only, non-empirical) are met. Inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using the probabilistic category learning (weather prediction) task. The task involves an explicit goal (predict rain vs shine) and requires participants to infer cue–outcome mappings and apply strategies to improve accuracy, which meets the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed inference and rule application). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM99), provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates in tables and figures, and reports BOLD fMRI results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the manuscript appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses task-based BOLD fMRI (PVSAT) involving rule-based arithmetic operations (serial addition) that require goal-directed processing, planning/sequencing and execution of operations, which fits the review's operational definition of problem solving. It includes healthy adult control participants and reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (controls), with activations normalized to MNI space and coordinates reported. DTI/FT analyses are additional but do not conflict with inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, healthy-group task effects are presented, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Full text appears complete. The study is a task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group analyses using SPM (voxelwise suprathreshold voxel counts), provides stereotactic coordinates for focal ROIs, and reports BOLD results (satisfies I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task is a modified Sternberg verbal working-memory/recognition task (encoding, delay, probe) assessing maintenance and retrieval, not a problem-solving task as defined (no goal-directed planning/sequencing or operations to derive novel solutions). Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Exclude on the basis that the cognitive task does not meet the review's problem-solving definition.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that requires participants to apply and search memory for stimulus–response rules to predict winners, which meets the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed rule evaluation, planning/selection of actions, and rule-conforming operations). The study uses whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (n=12), reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates in tables/figures, and analyzes BOLD signal (fMRI). Voxelwise results are presented in tables and figures. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is provided in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain group-level BOLD results in standardized (MNI) space and voxelwise coordinates. However, the paradigms are Theory of Mind (perspective taking/false-belief) and a stop-signal response inhibition task. These measure social cognition and motor inhibition, not a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., tasks requiring evaluation/planning/sequencing and execution to reach a previously unknown solution within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical, or similar rule frameworks). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. The study does satisfy I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that used a conditional/logical reasoning task requiring participants to apply logical rules (problem-solving within a logical framework). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (SPM8), with voxelwise results and peak coordinates (MNI normalization) and BOLD-based fMRI contrasts (e.g., LC vs BC) reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain neuroimaging studies of problem solving.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that used an equation-verification paradigm requiring goal-directed evaluation and retrieval/calculation to reach correct answers, satisfying the review's definition of problem solving. It reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses of BOLD fMRI data in healthy adult participants, and presents task-related activation loci (with figures/tables indicated) consistent with stereotactic reporting conventions for SPM analyses. The study also includes ROI analyses but not as the sole reported results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so content is complete for screening purposes.

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is an incentivized motor pursuit (chasing an artificial prey) emphasizing reward motivation, motor control, and procedural execution rather than explicit problem solving that requires identifying/evaluating a problem, planning or sequencing actions to derive a novel/correct solution within a rule-based framework (e.g., semantic, algebraic, logical). The full text is complete and the study does meet I6 (group whole-brain fMRI analysis), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., ROI-only). Therefore exclude because I5 is not met.

This study used a visuospatial judgment (angle discrimination) task that is a perceptual decision/discrimination paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined (i.e., requiring formulation of a goal followed by planning/sequencing or execution of operations to arrive at a novel or rule-based solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem solving task) is not met. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study with group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise/coordinate results (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Hence exclude due to failure to satisfy I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes a Tower of London (ToL) planning paradigm which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (explicit goal, planning/sequencing moves, executing operations under rules to arrive at a solution). Whole-brain, group-level analyses are reported (main effects and group comparisons), healthy adult controls are included, and BOLD fMRI contrasts and voxelwise results are reported in figures/tables (e.g., Table 3 and SPM results described). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This study does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). Although it is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results in MNI space (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task is a forced-choice preference selection between abstract value words reflecting moral/value orientation, not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm as defined in I5. Participants made spontaneous preference judgments rather than engaging in identifying/planning/sequencing actions or applying rule-based operations to reach a correct or novel solution. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because I5 is not satisfied; other inclusion criteria (I6,I7,I8,I9) are met.

The study is a task-based whole-brain fMRI investigation of social conformity using a perceptual dot-estimation task with minimal group manipulation. While it meets imaging-related criteria (whole-brain group analyses, MNI coordinates, BOLD analysis, and reporting of voxelwise results), it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in the review (no goal-directed planning/sequencing or execution of rule-based operations to derive a previously unknown solution). Instead, the task is perceptual estimation and social influence, not problem solving. Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the review's problem-solving task requirement (I5). The fMRI tasks are Theory of Mind (self-perspective inhibition) and a stop-signal response-inhibition task, which do not meet the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel or rule-based solution). The full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults reported), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm as defined). No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to failure to satisfy I5.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a modified beads probabilistic reasoning task that requires goal-directed evidence gathering and decision-making (evaluating information, planning when to stop, and executing responses), fitting the operational definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts (task blocks vs control; last vs preceding stimuli), provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activations, and includes ROI analyses but not exclusively. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9, and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (scanned N=20) that uses whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses and reports BOLD task-related activations. The task is a goal-directed mental-arithmetic paradigm requiring sequencing of operations, maintenance and integration of intermediate results, and execution of rule-based operations to arrive at correct answers, meeting the review’s definition of problem solving. Stereotactic coordinates are reported in Talairach space (Table 1 and figures). The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using arithmetic problems (multiplication and subtraction), which constitute problem-solving within an algebraic/arithmetic rule set. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM2, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables and figures), and reports BOLD/fMRI results (voxelwise cluster-level statistics). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, disease-only comparisons, non-empirical) are met.

The study is task-based fMRI with whole-brain/group-level analyses in healthy adults, reports BOLD effects and stereotactic coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, and I9). However, the task probes theory of mind/attention via story reading and likelihood judgments, not a problem-solving task as defined (no goal-directed planning, sequencing, or execution to arrive at a solution). Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on failure to meet I5 (problem-solving task).

Full text is complete. Study is task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (satisfies I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task is a sentence–picture matching task probing spatial language and frames of reference, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no explicit goal-driven problem solving, planning/sequencing operations, or novel solution generation). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: none. Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using two numerical tasks (number comparison and number bisection) that require rule-based operations to arrive at correct answers and therefore meet the review's problem-solving task definition. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses (healthy participants: OC-users, naturally cycling women, men) with cluster-level FDR correction, BOLD results, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related activations and effects. Voxelwise results are presented in the main text (and implied figures/tables). The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of problem solving (single-digit multiplication) in healthy adult participants that requires goal-directed, rule-based operations and sequencing (I5). The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adults (I6), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and explicitly normalizes data to MNI space and reports voxelwise cluster results (main text refers to stereotactic results and supplementary material), satisfying reporting of coordinates (I7) and allowing voxelwise results in figures/tables (I9). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary data are referenced. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the article does not clearly meet all required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI with math problems that qualify as rule-based problem solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy control group), I8 (BOLD-based fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space for task-related increases—no coordinate tables or explicit coordinates are present in the text provided), and the primary whole-brain results emphasize feedback/stress-related contrasts rather than explicit problem-solving (math) contrasts for healthy adults, so it is unclear that the paper reports the problem-solving task-related stereotactic coordinate results required for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete. Therefore I exclude on the basis of missing stereotactic coordinate reporting and unclear reporting of problem-solving (math) whole-brain coordinate results.

The study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). It uses a verbal working memory (Sternberg-like) and a control letter-reading task in chronic hemodialysis patients and controls; these tasks do not involve goal-driven problem solving, planning/sequencing or rule-based solution generation across domains. The full text is complete and reports whole-brain BOLD analyses with MNI coordinates and group-level effects, so it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore excluded because it fails to meet the key inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that reports whole-brain group analyses with MNI coordinates and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task is a symbolic magnitude-comparison (deciding which of two numbers is larger/smaller), which is a basic numerical judgment rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., having a goal that requires planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I5 not met; I6–I9 are met; no exclusion criteria met.

This study meets the meta-analysis objectives and all inclusion criteria. I5: The task required participants to extract rules and engage hypothesis-testing/explicit memory processes to classify patterns, satisfying the definition of problem solving (goal-directed rule extraction, evaluation, and execution). I6: Uses whole-brain random-effects group analyses in 18 healthy adults. I7: Data were spatially normalized to MNI space and voxel coordinates are reported. I8: Task-based BOLD fMRI responses (hemodynamic response) were analyzed. I9: Voxelwise results and coordinates are presented in tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no patient-only or group-comparison-only results, and it is empirical). Therefore include.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines cognitive processes engaged to evaluate and solve single-digit multiplication problems. The multiplication task requires goal-directed evaluation and execution of arithmetic operations (rule-based problem solving and strategy use), fitting the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (random-effects), uses BOLD fMRI, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and presents voxelwise results with appropriate statistical thresholds and tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient/age/gender-only comparisons, includes within-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a decision/problem-solving card task that requires goal-directed strategy formation, evaluation of outcomes, planning/sequencing choices, and executing rule-based selections to maximize reward. The paper reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses with cluster results and refers to tables of clusters in standardized atlas space (registration to an atlas and cluster lists are described), and voxelwise results are presented. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and none of the exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient/group-comparison-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task is a morality Implicit Association Test (IAT) requiring categorization and measuring implicit attitudes, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions to arrive at a previously unknown solution). The full text meets other inclusion criteria: I6 (task-based whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults, N=20), I7 (images normalized to Talairach space and the manuscript indicates stereotactic/voxelwise results are reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), and I9 (voxelwise results are indicated as available in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded on the basis of failure to satisfy I5.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in 20 healthy adult participants that investigates arithmetic tasks requiring goal-directed problem solving (calculating next terms in Simple/Linear/Quad conditions), involving planning/sequencing and execution of rule-based operations (recursive arithmetic). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides voxelwise activation results with stereotactic normalization to MNI space (coordinates reported/figures/tables). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group disease comparisons only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.
