The fMRI study reports a goal-directed task (count visible balls from either own or avatar perspective) that requires mental spatial transformation and execution of operations to arrive at a correct response, satisfying the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The study includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI analyses (I8). Task-related voxelwise results are presented in text/tables and ROI/whole-brain contrasts (I9). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper presents whole-brain results (not ROI-only), reports healthy-group task effects, and is an original empirical fMRI study. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-based neuroimaging studies of problem-solving across domains.

This study does not examine problem solving as defined in I5. It investigates autobiographical memory, prospection, and theory-of-mind using task-based fMRI in healthy adults. It meets I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adult participants), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures). It does NOT meet I5 because the tasks involve remembering, imagining future events, and inferring others' mental states rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded for not addressing the review objective (I5 not met).

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study of transitive inference (a reasoning/problem-solving task requiring participants to use learned relations to derive novel pairwise orderings). It reports group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adult participants (n=15), uses voxelwise statistics with Talairach coordinates (tables/figures), and presents BOLD %-change/rCBF-style results and thresholded activation maps. The task meets the problem-solving definition (goal-directed reasoning/manipulation of learned facts to arrive at novel solutions). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria below.

This is a PET study in healthy adults using the Montreal Card Sorting Task (MCST). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (MCST requires goal-directed rule identification, set-shifting and execution consistent with the provided problem-solving definition), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses across 8 healthy adults with within-subject contrasts), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (study does not report BOLD or rCBF; it is a neurotransmission PET ligand binding study [11C]FLB 457 measuring D2 receptor binding potential/dopamine release, not blood-oxygen-level-dependent signal or cerebral blood flow). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because I8 is required but not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study of mental arithmetic (3-operand calculation) in healthy adults, with voxelwise BOLD analyses and group-level contrasts. The task qualifies as a problem-solving paradigm (algebraic/arithmetic operations requiring goal-directed computation). The paper reports whole-brain SPM group analyses, stereotactic coordinates (MNI transformed to Talairach), and VBM structural results; voxelwise results are described and cluster-level corrected. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects in healthy adults).

The study investigates scene construction and imagination, not a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined by the review (no requirement to identify/plan/execute actions to reach a goal or solve a rule-based problem). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I5. It does meet other inclusion criteria: task-based whole-brain fMRI with group-level analyses (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and voxelwise results are available in the text/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (BOLD) using a modified beads probabilistic decision-making task that requires participants to achieve a goal (identify source lake) by evaluating evidence and choosing whether to sample more information—meeting the review’s operational definition of problem-solving. It includes whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adult controls (one-sample and two-sample tests), reports stereotactic coordinates for activations (MNI/Talairach), and presents BOLD results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, is empirical).

Although this is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that uses whole-brain random-effects analyses and examines causal/scientific reasoning (which meets I5, I6, and I8), the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) or present voxelwise coordinate tables/figures in the supplied content. Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting task-related increases as stereotactic coordinate results) is not satisfied based on the provided material. Because all inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not met, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered in the provided text.

While this is a whole-brain, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults reporting stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and group-level analyses, the task is a perceptual decision-making/social information integration task (guessing a flashed stimulus location) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (no goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions or critical-thinking operations to derive a novel solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review criteria: participants performed goal-directed, rule-based mental transformations (transposition and reversal) to determine whether a target melody matched a transformed sample, constituting a problem-solving operation as defined in I5. Whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses are reported (I6) with BOLD contrasts (I8). Images/analyses were transformed to MNI/ICBM stereotaxic space and voxelwise results/conjunctions are reported (I7,I9). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is sufficient for extraction. No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. The study uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain analyses in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results; however, the experimental paradigm is a working memory (listening/reading span and word-recognition) task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed evaluation/planning/sequencing to reach a solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), I9 (qualifying voxelwise results are available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is working memory, not problem-solving). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Given that ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I5 is not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and a goal-directed Internet search task that meets the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). It also includes whole-brain group analyses (I6) and BOLD measurement (I8). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the manuscript text/tables/figures supplied, so inclusion criterion I7 is not met. I9 (availability of voxelwise results in tables/figures/supplement) is also not clearly satisfied in the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because all inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is missing in the provided full text, the study must be excluded.

This is a single-subject (one 16-year-old) EEG/fMRI case study of mental addition. While the study uses task-based whole-brain fMRI with BOLD analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates (satisfying I5, I7, I8, I9), it does NOT include any group-level effects in healthy adults (no group of healthy adult participants). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (doesn't include any healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Exclusion IDs met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no group-level healthy adult data).

This is a whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD effects and group-level analyses, but it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in the review. The experimental paradigm concerns literary comprehension, poetic recognition, and reappraisal of meaning (interpreting text), rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing actions or operations within a formal rule set to arrive at a correct or novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results indicated as available in figures/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based problem-solving as defined), I7 (stereotactic coordinates are not explicitly reported in the provided full text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study investigates rtfMRI working memory (WM) feedback training, not problem-solving as defined in the review (no goal-directed problem-solving/planning/execution across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule-sets). It does include healthy adult participants and whole-brain analyses (group ICA), reports stereotactic ROI coordinates (MNI), and uses BOLD fMRI data, but it does not meet the core inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are directly triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain ICA analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in standardized space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates available in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is working memory training/feedback, not problem-solving). Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults that reports whole-brain BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) and group-level analyses; however, the experimental task probes theory-of-mind (attribution of intentions/beliefs in social cartoons), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a correct/novel solution). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the meta-analysis definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

While the study meets multiple neuroimaging reporting requirements (group-level whole-brain random-effects analysis, stereotactic MNI coordinates, and BOLD fMRI results), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in the review. The experimental paradigm assesses personal involvement and information-search behavior (deciding whether to view more product information), rather than a goal-oriented problem-solving activity requiring planning/sequencing of rule-based operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a defined/problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet I5: the task is causality judgement (evaluating whether motion implies causality), not a problem-solving task as defined (having an explicit goal, requiring planning/sequencing operations or executing rule-based solutions to reach an unknown solution). It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/in supplements). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore exclude because key inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied.

This study is task-based fMRI in healthy participants and reports whole-brain BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates; however, the experimental paradigm (mini-Ultimatum Game) probes social fairness/intentionality and decision-making rather than a defined problem-solving task as specified by inclusion criterion I5. Therefore it does not meet the review’s required definition of problem solving. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain analyses including healthy adult participants), I7 (reports coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results available in text/figures). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I5 (does not examine a problem-solving task per the meta-analysis definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity in abstinent alcohol-dependent patients (clinical sample) using survival analysis to predict relapse. It does not study a problem-solving task (fails I5) and does not include healthy adult participants or report healthy-group task effects (fails I6). The study does report voxelwise whole-brain coordinates in MNI (I7), uses BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise results in the main text/figures (I9). Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the paper does not include any healthy-group task effects (only a clinical group). Therefore it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review.

The study used task-based whole-brain fMRI (BOLD) in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates, but the in-scanner tasks are working memory (span) tasks rather than problem-solving tasks as defined. Although Raven’s Progressive Matrices (a problem-solving/reasoning test) was administered behaviorally outside the scanner, the neuroimaging data do not probe problem solving. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task-based fMRI/PET of a problem-solving task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study uses task-based BOLD imaging in healthy adult participants (n=25) performing an arithmetic equation-verification task and an operation-span (OSPAN) complex span task. The arithmetic condition requires evaluating equations and executing arithmetic operations (semantic/algebraic rule-based processing), which fits the meta-analysis definition of problem-solving (goal-directed evaluation and operation sequencing). The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (warped to MNI space), ROI and whole-brain contrasts (task>baseline; OSPAN>Arithmetic), and provides stereotactic-based results and cluster tables consistent with reporting in MNI coordinates. Thus it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

The study includes a task (mental arithmetic) that meets the review's problem-solving definition: participants have a goal (add presented numbers and choose the correct sum) and must perform rule-based operations (arithmetic) to reach a correct solution. It is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (meditators and controls), with group-level random-effects analyses and whole-brain exploratory analyses reported. Stereotactic coordinates are provided in MNI space, and the imaging modality is task BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are reported (tables/coordinates and text). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Although the arithmetic task was used as a control for a meditation study, the task nonetheless qualifies as a problem-solving task for the meta-analysis objective. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting task-related BOLD effects with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, the experimental paradigm examines risky decision making (preferential vs. judgment-based choices about monetary gambles) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., having a goal and requiring planning, sequencing, or executing operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution). The tasks involve preference selection and estimating certainty equivalents, not identification and performance of critical thinking processes to solve a delimited problem. Therefore I5 is not satisfied, so the study must be excluded despite meeting I6–I9. Full text appears complete.

The study does not meet the review’s core inclusion criteria. While it reports whole-brain fMRI results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and BOLD analyses (I7, I8) and presents voxelwise results in-text (I9), it does not investigate a clear problem-solving task as defined by I5—the Hayling Sentence Completion Test is a verbal initiation/language/constraint task rather than an explicit problem-solving/planning/sequencing task. Crucially, participants are young individuals at familial high genetic risk for schizophrenia (unaffected relatives), not a sample of healthy adult individuals as required by I6. No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are directly triggered, but failure to meet I5 and I6 necessitates exclusion. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults reporting stereotactic coordinates, the experimental task is a two-digit number magnitude comparison (decide which of two numbers is larger). This is a perceptual/cognitive magnitude-comparison task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (which requires goal-directed planning, sequencing, evaluation, or execution of operations to arrive at a solution beyond a single-step comparison). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. Inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 are met (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults; stereotactic coordinates reported; BOLD fMRI analysis). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). The task contrasts emotional and cognitive perspective-taking (theory-of-mind/empathy), not goal-directed problem solving involving planning/plausible rule-based operations to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses on healthy adults using SPM), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it fails to meet I5 (problem-solving task).

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in MNI space, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed search, planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a solution). The experiment probes retrieval/representation of action knowledge (how vs why) and mentalizing, not critical-thinking/planning operations to achieve a goal or generate solutions. Therefore I5 is not met; I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that examines cognitive processes requiring rule learning, memory search, hypothesis testing and application of stimulus–response rules (Exp. 2 involves training, learning, exploring and testing rule sets), which fit the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed evaluation, planning/updating task representations, and executing rule-based operations to obtain correct outcomes). The paper reports group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses using BOLD-sensitive EPI (3T), provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates in tables and figures, and reports voxelwise parametric and main-task effects. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical human data).

The study does not meet all inclusion criteria required for this meta-analysis. Although it reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise results/figures with coordinates (I9), it fails to meet I6: there is no whole-brain task-based group-level functional analysis — functional data were restricted to a brainstem-centered slab (SN/VTA) with small-volume correction rather than an unrestricted whole-brain analysis. It also does not clearly meet I5: the task is a reinforcement-based sequential investment/decision-making task rather than an explicit problem-solving task as defined (planning/sequencing to reach a novel correct solution across domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of number comparison and digit identification in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (MNI). However, the experimental tasks are basic numeric magnitude comparison and digit identification rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., tasks requiring goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing, or executing operations to reach a solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (API error returned); core methods/results unavailable, so I cannot verify required inclusion criteria. Based on available metadata, there is no evidence that this is a whole-brain, task-based fMRI or PET study of problem solving in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be verified: I5 (task-based fMRI or PET problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate results reported), I8 (BOLD or rCBF analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results available). No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the available information (exclusion_criteria_applied: []). Excluding because full text is incomplete and thus ALL inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed.

This is an fMRI study of everyday moral decision-making (choices between moral vs. hedonistic options). While it includes whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The task involves moral reasoning/decision-making and affective appraisal rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires planning/sequencing operations within a rule-defined framework to arrive at a correct or novel solution. No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., ROI-only, between-group-only, non-empirical). Therefore excluded because it fails to meet I5 (problem-solving task).

The study is an fMRI task of decision-making under uncertainty in an aviation-simulation landing task. It meets I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adult participants), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), and I9 (voxelwise results and tables reported). However, it does not meet I5: the task is a binary decision/risk-taking task (landing vs. go-around) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (involving goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore the study does not address the review’s problem-solving construct and must be excluded.

Although this is a whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD analyses, the task investigated (mental rotation and perspective taking) is a perceptual/spatial transformation task rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing or critical-thinking operations to reach a solution). The study does not involve identifying or performing critical thinking processes, planning/sequencing actions, or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a (novel) solution in the sense required by inclusion criterion I5. Therefore I5 is not met. All other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study does not investigate problem solving as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations to solve a problem). It examines mental state decoding (theory of mind) from eye-region stimuli, a social-perceptual task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes) rather than tasks requiring problem identification, planning, or rule-based solution execution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task-based whole-brain fMRI group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise/results provided in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not study a defined problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Consequently, exclude due to failure to meet I5.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that contrasts decision-making in Prisoner’s Dilemma (PD) and Stag Hunt (SH). The tasks involve goal-directed strategizing (maximizing monetary payoff) and, for the PD, dominance-solvable iterative reasoning—meeting the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level GLM results in healthy adults (I6), provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates for task-related activations (I7), and reports BOLD analyses (I8). Coordinate results and cluster maps are reported in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only results, no patient-group-only contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study includes a clearly defined problem-solving task (the Math task: serial addition/subtraction with a goal to compute a correct result using rule-based operations and adaptive difficulty), meeting the review's operational definition of problem solving. It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants (N=34 across cohorts), and provides stereotaxic coordinates of activation peaks (Talairach/MNI) and voxelwise maps. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. The primary paper emphasizes the Story>Math contrast (semantic processing), but the Math task was explicitly modeled and analyzed in whole-brain regressors, so problem-solving-related activation data should be present or derivable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical original data). Full text appears complete. Caveat: math/task contrasts are not the paper's main focus, which slightly reduces confidence but does not preclude inclusion per criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition / Theory of Mind using a naturalistic video-based MASC paradigm, not a problem‑solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule‑based operations to find a solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem solving task) is NOT met. The study does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using numerical problem-like tasks (number comparison and number bisection) that require goal-directed operations and rule-based evaluation to arrive at correct solutions. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM5), thresholded cluster results, and stereotactic coordinates (e.g., Precuneus [-15, -39, 33]; ACC [-6, 24, 18]) in MNI space. BOLD fMRI analyses are clearly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual stimulation with attentional modulation (checkerboard with attend/ignore/discriminate letter-detection). While it includes whole-brain group analyses, stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD-based results, the experimental tasks (attentional modulation and letter detection) do not constitute a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or critical-thinking operations across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Study is a complete full text.

Excluded because the task studied is moral decision-making/ToM/empathy, not a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5 not met). The study does meet other methodological inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults (I6), BOLD fMRI (I8), and the manuscript indicates voxelwise results/tables/supplementary are available (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines cognitive processes involved in solving multiple-choice electric-circuit problems. The task requires participants to evaluate circuit configurations and decide correctness, matching the operational definition of problem solving (goal-directed evaluation and rule-based operations to reach correct answers). The study reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses using SPM8, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for task contrasts (e.g., Uncertainty>Certainty, LC>OE), and presents voxelwise results in tables and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, image acquisition, GLM), Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is a methods/validation paper on complexity (Hurst exponent) estimation applied to various fMRI tasks (rest, movie viewing, emotional faces, auditory anticipation). It includes whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates (e.g., MNI = -64, -20, 2), so it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, none of the reported tasks constitute a problem-solving paradigm as defined (goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Hence the study must be excluded from the review.

Exclusion: E3 (study reports only ROI-based analyses). Inclusion met: I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI). Inclusion not met: I5 (does not examine a problem-solving task as defined; it contrasts number vs. letter comparison rather than planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution), I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis reported; analyses are ROI-focused), I7 (no whole-brain task-related stereotactic coordinate results appropriate for meta-analysis). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates cognitive processes requiring problem solving (deriving sorting rules via trial-and-error, hypothesis generation, feedback integration, and behavioral adaptation). The paper reports group-level random-effects analyses from 14 healthy volunteers, provides whole-brain stereotactic coordinates (MNI, with Talairach conversion) in tables/figures, and uses BOLD fMRI results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) and no exclusion criteria are met.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in standardized space (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task (causal verbal fluency / free association / phonological fluency) is a semantic retrieval/verbal fluency paradigm rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined in I5. The task requires generation of associated or causal words but does not require identifying/planning or executing a sequence of operations to reach a correct or novel solution within a rule-based problem framework. Authors describe aspects as ‘reasoning,’ but the paradigm lacks the structured, goal-oriented problem solving (evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, rule-based operations to arrive at a solution) required by I5. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults present), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 — the experimental task is Theory of Mind / false-belief reasoning (mentalizing/social cognition), not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing/execution to arrive at an unknown solution across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical domains). Therefore the study does not address the review's target construct (problem solving). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of non-conscious visual working memory and delayed orientation discrimination; it does not investigate problem-solving as defined in I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing or performing critical thinking to generate novel solutions across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule sets). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. It does satisfy other methodological criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and includes BOLD analyses (I8); voxelwise results are reported (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (meets I6, I8) and reports group-level whole-brain results with stereotactic peak/beta data (figures/supplementary tables imply coordinates; meets I7 and I9), the experimental paradigm is an instrumental visuomotor associative learning / trial-and-error conditioning task. It does not involve the type of problem-solving defined in the review (i.e., tasks requiring critical evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions, or application of explicit rule-based/semantic/algebraic/logical operations to arrive at a novel solution). The task primarily probes stimulus–response learning, performance monitoring and habit formation rather than domain-general or domain-specific problem solving. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task as defined) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). The fMRI task is a theory-of-mind (mental state reasoning) Person-Description/False-Belief paradigm (thoughts/emotions vs appearance), which does not involve goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations, or rule-based solution generation required by the meta-analysis definition of problem solving. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain analyses with group-level effects in healthy adult individuals are reported), I7 (results reported in MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), I9 (voxelwise/whole-brain results presented in main text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria applied: none (no E3–E6 violations). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of probabilistic monetary decision-making (expected value, reward magnitude, temporal-difference prediction errors) and does not investigate problem-solving as defined (goal-directed identification/planning/sequencing to derive solutions under semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical or similar rule frameworks). Although the study is empirical, uses healthy adult participants, reports whole-brain group analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, and BOLD results, it does not meet the required task definition for problem solving (I5). Therefore it must be excluded. No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and random-effects analyses. The tasks include deductive reasoning (DR) requiring logical inference to determine hat color given constraints, which meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical operations). Whole-brain contrasts (e.g., DR vs. PC, MI vs. DR) are reported with cluster-level correction and coordinates; BOLD analyses and voxelwise results are presented. Participants are healthy adults. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The experimental tasks involved passive observation of toolmaking videos with instructions to ‘imagine’ continuing the action or to ‘evaluate’ success, rather than requiring participants to perform explicit problem-solving (i.e., generate/plan and execute solutions to a presented problem under a rule set). The study does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it is excluded due to failure to satisfy I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates causal-attribution judgments requiring participants to identify appropriate causes for observed events (a goal-directed evaluative/inferential task). It includes whole-brain group-level analyses (random effects), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space, and uses BOLD fMRI analyses. The experimental task requires goal-directed evaluation (determine causes), i.e., critical thinking/inference consistent with the review's problem-solving definition. Full article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text.

This is an fMRI study of theory-of-mind (ToM) processing (false belief, desire, human action stories) in healthy adults with whole-brain, random-effects BOLD analyses and reported stereotactic coordinates. However, it does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review (a task with an explicit goal requiring planning/critical thinking to devise and execute a solution within a defined rule framework). The tasks are social-cognitive attribution and comprehension of mental states, not goal-directed problem solving, planning, or rule-based solution execution. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete.

This study does not investigate problem-solving as defined by I5. The experimental tasks focus on self-construal priming (pronoun detection) and subsequent resting-state measures; the calculation blocks served only as a baseline parity/odd–even judgment and are not presented or analyzed as a problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing or solving novel problems. The paper does meet several technical inclusion criteria (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults; stereotactic coordinates in MNI; BOLD fMRI analyses; voxelwise results reported), but it fails I5 (task-based problem solving). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=20) using a two-armed instrumental learning task in which participants had a goal (earn snacks) and had to learn/figure out which action led to reward (planning/choosing actions to reach a goal). The study reports whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses with voxelwise BOLD results reported in MNI coordinates (e.g., right dlPFC peak 44,25,37) and includes dynamic causal modeling and additional whole-brain contrasts. Thus it meets criteria for a problem-solving-like task under the review’s definition, includes whole-brain group effects, reports stereotactic coordinates, and uses BOLD fMRI. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults and includes an explicit mental-calculation localizer (silent subtraction) that constitutes a problem-solving task (applying arithmetic rules to reach a solution). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed and reported, with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD contrasts (calculation > sentence comprehension). Healthy adult participants (n=14) were used. Thus it meets I5 (problem-solving task: mental calculation), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Full-text is complete. Exclusion rationale: No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results presented in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does NOT examine problem-solving as defined — tasks require participants to judge communicative vs. strategic rationality in scenarios, a moral/social judgment/assessment task rather than goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a solution). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I5.

The study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by criterion I5. The fMRI task involved prosodic speech production and a Rest vs Speech contrast, not goal-directed problem solving (no planning/sequencing to reach a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain contrast was performed to identify PMC and mPFC clusters), I7 (results reported in MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise/group results indicated and coordinates provided). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study does not examine problem-solving as defined in I5. The reported tasks (physical distance judgment, social-distance compatibility judgments, and social-feature judgements) require perceptual and social-evaluative comparisons, not goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing actions, or executing operations to arrive at a novel solution. The paper does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults, n=24), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise coordinate results presented in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I5 (problem-solving task).

While this is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes a calculation (subtraction) task meeting the review definition of a problem-solving operation (I5), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and provides voxelwise results in figures/tables (I9), it does NOT provide whole-brain coverage/analysis. Image acquisition covered only 18 axial slices limited to parietal and most prefrontal cortex, explicitly excluding orbitofrontal, lower temporal, and occipital cortices. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (requires at least one whole-brain analysis with group-level effects). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion is based on missing I6.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study in adults using an evidence-accumulation/decision-making paradigm in which participants have the goal of identifying which deck produced observed draws (explicit goal, sequential evidence, inference to a correct solution). The task fits the operational definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed evaluation/decision based on rules/probabilities). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise BOLD analyses with group-level effects including within-group results for healthy controls, provides stereotactic (MNI) coordinates in tables/figures (e.g., Table IV), and reports BOLD (fMRI) results. Voxelwise results are provided in tables and supplemental materials. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical original data). Full text is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a PET investigation of Stroop task performance (selective attention/interference/inhibition), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). It does include whole-brain, group-level PET analyses in healthy adults (meets I6) and reports rCBF task-related analyses (meets I8). The provided full text does not present stereotactic peak coordinates in Talairach or MNI space in the excerpt available, so I7 cannot be confirmed (treated as not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task (I5) and stereotactic coordinate reporting (I7) is not confirmed in the provided text. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This fMRI study does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review (I5). The task manipulated number of choice options and social equality of opportunity; it did not require participants to formulate a plan, sequence actions, or apply rule-based operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution. It does, however, meet other methodological inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinate reporting in MNI space (I7), BOLD analysis (I8), and acceptable reporting of voxelwise results (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that performs whole-brain BOLD analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates; however, it does not study a problem-solving task as defined in the review. The experimental task is a serial reaction/time image-identification paradigm designed to probe sequential prediction and associative learning (reaction time modulation by learned transition probabilities), rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm requiring participants to evaluate, plan or generate solutions to a specified problem. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. The manuscript does meet I6 (group whole-brain analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results in figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are applicable. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based solely on failure to satisfy I5.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adult participants that used a logical reasoning task meeting the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical reasoning with rule-based responses). Whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses were performed at the group level (INHIB and LOGIC groups). The study reports regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) task-related analyses and refers to peak (stereotactic) coordinates and conjunction maps (voxelwise results presented in maps/figures), satisfying requirements for reporting standardized coordinates/voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, clinical-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core data appear present.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study uses task-based fMRI in healthy volunteers and reports activations, so it meets I6 (group whole-brain effects in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis). However, the task is empathy/forgiveness social judgment, not a problem-solving task as defined (does not involve goal-directed problem-solving, planning/sequencing to reach a solution), so I5 is not met. I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) cannot be confirmed from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the primary inclusion criterion I5, and the full text is incomplete.

This study does not meet the review’s problem-solving scope and does not provide a clear whole-brain task effect in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI in tables), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a probabilistic decision-making/beads task focusing on probabilistic reasoning and reward/salience processing rather than a defined problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning/sequencing operations as specified), I6 (the paper does not clearly report a whole-brain, group-level task effect specifically for the healthy adult group alone — reported ‘across-group’ (combined sample) effects and group comparisons, with ROI group differences; thus it fails to provide a healthy-only whole-brain task activation). Exclusion criteria applied: E5 (the study does not provide a qualifying healthy-group task effect; the reported whole-brain task effects are across the combined sample rather than a healthy-controls-only group effect, and primary between-group contrasts and ROI comparisons are emphasized). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult controls and high-risk relatives that reports whole-brain BOLD results in MNI space. However, the experimental task (Hayling Sentence Completion / verbal initiation/verbal fluency) primarily probes language and executive fluency under constraint rather than multi-step problem solving, planning/sequencing, or rule-based operations across domains as defined by the review. Therefore it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (task is not a qualifying problem-solving task per the review definition). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20 after exclusion) that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates. The experimental paradigm requires goal-directed, rule-governed sequential decision-making: participants aim to maximize monetary yield (explicit goal), must evaluate noisy evidence about bandit payoffs, plan/sequence accepts or rejects across trials (rule-in vs rule-out), and execute rule-conforming actions to achieve better outcomes. The paper presents whole-brain results (corrected), coordinates in MNI space, and BOLD analyses, satisfying I6–I9. The task meets the problem-solving definition (evaluating the problem, planning/sequencing actions under rules, and executing operations to reach a better solution), supporting I5. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain voxel-wise analyses and stereotactic MNI coordinates of BOLD effects. However, the experimental task is reversal learning (reward/punishment contingency updating), which does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning/sequencing/operations to derive a solution within an explicit rule set). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Summary of criteria: inclusion met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results presented). inclusion not met: I5 (task is reversal learning, not a problem-solving task per provided definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain analyses and BOLD results (meets I6 and I8). However, the experimental task is moral judgment/decision-making (personal vs. impersonal moral dilemmas) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution), so it does not meet I5. Additionally, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate results (Talairach/MNI) or clearly indicate that such coordinates are available in tables/figures/supplement (I7 and I9 not met based on the provided content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines cognitive operations involving arithmetic verification (algebraic rule-based operations) within an operation span (dual-task) paradigm. It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (random-effects SPM99), provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space, and BOLD signal (% signal change) analyses. Participants are healthy adults and results include task-related activations and coordinates in tables/figures. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that includes classic problem-solving/fluid-reasoning tasks (paper folding, matrix reasoning, letter sets) and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses. Thus I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD analysis) are satisfied. However, in the provided full text there is no explicit reporting of stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) or coordinate tables/labels for task-related activations; I7 is not met based on the available content. Because all inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not satisfied in the provided full text, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the study does not provide any healthy-group task-related neuroimaging effect. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI/PET neuroimaging study of problem solving — PET here measured presynaptic Fdopa uptake at rest rather than task-evoked activity), I6 (no whole-brain, group-level task effects reported for healthy adults), I7 (no task-related stereotactic coordinates for BOLD/rCBF activations reported), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF task analysis — molecular Fdopa uptake was measured). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the requirement for task-based whole-brain neuroimaging of problem-solving in healthy adults and includes no healthy-group task effect (E5).

The study is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and random-effects group analyses. However, it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). The tasks are numerical magnitude judgments, comparisons, and approximate calculation/estimation, which are numerical cognition tasks rather than domain-general problem-solving tasks per the provided definition. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of Theory of Mind (false belief) processing, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review. Although the study meets several methodological inclusion criteria (I6: whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults; I7: reports MNI stereotactic coordinates; I8: BOLD analyses reported; I9: voxelwise results/tables provided), it does not meet I5. The task isolates computation and selection of others' vs. one's own beliefs and examines social cognitive processes (decoupling, temporoparietal and medial prefrontal connectivity), rather than a problem-solving paradigm requiring goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to derive a novel solution (e.g., semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical problem solving).
